(p-3) Surat al-Furqan.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion (al-Furqan) upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds.﴾ In this noble verse, Allah, majestic and exalted, mentions that He ﴿sent down the Criterion﴾, which is this Great Qur'an, ﴿upon His servant﴾, who is Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾, meaning a warner. We have repeatedly stated that warning (indhar) is informing accompanied by threat and intimidation, that every warning is an informing, but not every informing is a warning, as we explained at the beginning of Surat al-A'raf.

This noble verse indicates the universality of his (ﷺ) mission to the black and the red, and to jinn and humankind, since all of them are included in His saying, ﴿a warner to the worlds﴾.

This meaning indicated by this noble verse is clarified in other verses, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: O mankind, I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾.

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a comprehensive messenger to mankind﴾ [al-A'raf: 158], meaning: We sent you to mankind comprehensively, that is, all of them.

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "What thing is greatest in testimony?" Say: "Allah is witness between me and you. And this Qur'an was revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches"﴾ [al-An'am: 19].

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass through; you will not pass except with authority﴾ ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [al-Rahman: 33–43].

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [mention] when We directed to you a company of the jinn listening to the Qur'an. And when they attended it, they said, "Listen attentively." And when it was concluded, they went back to their people as warners. They said, "O our people, we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what was before it, guiding to the truth and to a straight path. O our people, respond to the caller of Allah and believe in him; He will forgive you of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment. And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah will not cause [Him] to fail on earth"﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 29–32].

Regarding the meaning of His saying, "Blessed (tabaraka)," there are sayings among the scholars. Al-Qurtubi said: "Tabaraka has been disputed as to its meaning. Al-Farra' said: in Arabic it means 'glorified,' and both are for greatness. Al-Zajjaj said: tabaraka is of the form tafa'ala from barakah (blessing). He said: the meaning of barakah is abundance of every good thing. It was said: tabaraka means 'exalted.' It was said: 'His gift is exalted,' meaning it increased and abounded. It was said: the meaning is that His bounty endures and remains." Al-Nahhas said: "This is the most preferable in linguistics and derivation, from barak al-shay' when it remains firm, and from it comes barak al-jamal and al-tayr 'ala al-ma' (the camel and the bird kneeling on the water), meaning it endured and remained." End of the relevant point from al-Qurtubi's words.

Abu Hayyan said in al-Bahr al-Muhit: Ibn Abbas said: "Tabaraka: He has never ceased and never will cease." Al-Khalil said: "He is glorified (tamajjada)." Al-Dahhak said: "He is magnified (ta'azzama)." Al-Asma'i related: "Tabarakt 'alaykum (I have been blessed over you)" from the saying of an Arab who ascended a hill and said that to his companions, meaning: I have been exalted and elevated. In these sayings, tabaraka is an attribute of essence (sifat dhat). Ibn Abbas also said, as did al-Hasan and al-Nakha'i: it is from barakah, which is increase in good coming from Him. So the meaning is: His good and His gift increased and abounded, and according to this it is an attribute of action (sifat fi'l). End of the relevant point from Abu Hayyan's words.

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him and forgive him, says: The most apparent meaning of tabaraka according to the language in which the Qur'an was revealed is that it is of the form tafa'ala from barakah, as Ibn Jarir al-Tabari affirmed. According to this, the meaning of tabaraka is: blessings and goods have abounded from Him. This necessitates His greatness and His being exalted above everything unbecoming of His perfection and majesty, because He alone, from whom blessings and goods come and who bestows provision upon people, is the One singular in greatness and in deserving sincere worship. And that from which no blessing or good or provision comes, such as idols and all other things worshipped besides Allah, cannot validly be worshipped, and worshipping it is disbelief that leads to eternal abiding in the fire of Hell. Allah, exalted is He, has pointed to this in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you any provision; so seek provision from Allah, and worship Him, and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 17].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they worship besides Allah that which possesses for them no provision from the heavens or the earth at all, and they are unable﴾ [al-Nahl: 73].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He feeds but is not fed﴾ [al-An'am: 14].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me. Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 57–58].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who shows you His signs and sends down for you provision from the sky; but none is mindful except one who turns back [to Him]. So invoke Allah, sincere to Him in religion, although the disbelievers dislike it﴾ [Ghafir: 13–14].

A NOTE.

Know that His saying "tabaraka" is a rigid verb that does not conjugate, so no imperfect (mudari') form comes from it, nor a verbal noun (masdar), nor an active participle (ism al-fa'il), nor anything else. It is among the things specific to Allah, exalted is He, so it is not said of anyone else as "tabaraka," contrary to what was reported earlier from al-Asma'i. Attributing tabaraka to His saying ﴿who sent down the Criterion﴾ indicates that His sending down the Criterion upon His servant is among the greatest blessings, goods and favors that He has bestowed upon His creation, as we explained at the beginning of Surat al-Kahf, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Praise be to Allah who sent down upon His servant the Book﴾ [al-Kahf: 1], and we mentioned the verses that indicate this. The Arabs' usage of tabaraka attributed to Allah, exalted is He, is well known in their speech, and among it is the saying of al-Tirimmah:

"You are blessed; none gives what You have withheld, and none withholds what You have given, O Lord."

And the saying of another:

"Those evenings of the sanctuary will not return to us ever, as long as the green acacia puts forth leaves."

"Nor will that time which has passed return. You are blessed; whatever You decree comes to pass, and to You is thanks."

We have already cited the last witness in Surat al-Anbiya', in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And [Yunus] thought that We would not decree upon him﴾ [al-Anbiya': 87].

His saying: "al-Furqan" means this Great Qur'an. It is a verbal noun (masdar) to which the alif and nun have been added, like al-kufran, al-tughyan and al-ruj-han. This verbal noun is used to mean the active participle, because the meaning of its being a furqan is that it separates between truth and falsehood, and between right guidance and error. Some scholars said: the verbal noun al-furqan is used with the meaning of the passive participle (ism al-maf'ul), because it was sent down in parts, and was not sent down all at once.

The proponents of this view cite His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [it is] a Qur'an which We have separated (faraqnahu) that you might recite it to the people over a long period. And We have sent it down progressively﴾ [al-Isra': 106], and His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not revealed to him all at once?" Thus [it is] that We may strengthen thereby your heart; and We have spaced it in gradual order﴾ [al-Furqan: 32]. And His saying in this noble verse, "nazzala" with the intensive form, indicates the frequency of its sending down, being revealed in stages. Some scholars said: this is also indicated by His saying at the beginning of Surat Al 'Imran: ﴿He has sent down upon you the Book in truth, confirming that which was before it, and He revealed the Torah and the Gospel﴾ [Al 'Imran: 3]. They said: He expressed the sending down of the Qur'an with "nazzala" in the intensive form, because of the frequency of its sending down. As for the Torah and the Gospel, He expressed their sending down with "anzala," which does not indicate multiplicity, because they were sent down as a whole at one time. Some verses did not take into account the multiplicity of the Qur'an's sending down, (p-6) such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Praise be to Allah who sent down upon His servant the Book﴾ and so on [al-Kahf: 1]. As for His saying in this noble verse, ﴿upon His servant﴾, some scholars said: mentioning the attribute of servanthood alongside the sending down of the Criterion indicates that servanthood to Allah is the most noble of attributes. We have explained this at the beginning of Surat Bani Isra'il.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 2:

The Almighty's saying ﴿He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, who has not taken a son, and who has no partner in the dominion, and who created everything and determined it with precise determination﴾. His saying: ﴿to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "Him who" in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down﴾. Some of them said: it is in the nominative case by way of praise (madh), and some of them said: it is in the accusative case by way of praise. In this noble verse, the Majestic and Exalted praised Himself with five matters, which are decisive proofs of His greatness and of His sole entitlement to having worship sincerely devoted to Him. The first of them: that He is the One to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth.

The second: that He has not taken a son, glorified and exalted is He far above that.

The third: that there is no partner to Him in His dominion.

The fourth: that He is the Creator of everything.

The fifth: that He determined everything He created with precise determination. These five matters mentioned in this noble verse have come clarified in other verses.

As for the first of them, namely that to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, it has come clarified in many verses:

• Like His saying, exalted is He, in Surat "al-Ma'idah": ﴿Do you not know that Allah—to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth?﴾ and the rest of the verse [al-Ma'idah: 40].

• And His saying, exalted is He, in Surat "al-Nur": ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the final return﴾ [al-Nur: 42].

• And His saying: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion, and those you invoke other than Him do not possess even a date-seed's membrane﴾ and the rest of the verse [Fatir: 13]. In all the verses in which the Majestic and Exalted mentioned that to Him belongs dominion, the dominion in them encompasses the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and other than that.

• Like His saying: ﴿Say, "O Allah, Owner of dominion"﴾ and the rest of the verse [Al 'Imran: 26].

• And His saying: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion﴾ and the rest of the verse [al-Mulk: 1].

• And His saying: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is for Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ghafir: 16].

• And His saying: ﴿And His is the dominion on the day the Horn is blown﴾ and the rest of the verse [al-An'am: 73].

• And His saying: ﴿Owner of the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Fatihah: 4].

The verses indicating that He possesses the dominion of everything are very numerous and well known.

As for the second matter, namely that He, exalted is He, has not taken a son, it has come clarified in many verses:

• Like His saying: ﴿He neither begets nor is He begotten﴾ ﴿and there is not to Him any equivalent—anyone﴾ [al-Ikhlas: 3–4].

• And His saying: ﴿And that He—exalted is the majesty of our Lord—has not taken a companion or a son﴾ and the rest of the verse [al-Jinn: 3].

• And His saying: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth; how could He have a son when there is not for Him a companion?﴾ and the rest of the verse [al-An'am: 101].

• And His saying: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Certainly you have produced something monstrous. The heavens nearly rupture from it, the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son. There is no one in the heavens and earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ [Maryam: 88–93].

• And His saying: ﴿And to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son." They have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers. Enormous is the word that comes out of their mouths; they say not except a lie﴾ [al-Kahf: 4–5].

• And His saying: ﴿Has your Lord then favored you with sons and taken for Himself from the angels females? Indeed, you say a terrible saying﴾ [al-Isra': 40].

• And His saying: ﴿Allah has not taken any son, and there was not with Him any god﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they describe﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 91].

The verses similar to that are numerous and well known, and we have already presented that at several places in this blessed Book, in Surat "al-Kahf" and elsewhere.

As for the third matter, namely that He, exalted is He, has no partner in the dominion, it has come clarified in other than this place:

• Like His saying, exalted is He, at the end of Surat "Bani Isra'il": ﴿And say, "Praise is for Allah, who has not taken a son and has not had a partner in dominion"﴾ and the rest of the verse [al-Isra': 111].

• And His saying, exalted is He, in Surat "Saba'": ﴿Say, "Call upon those you claim besides Allah. They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, and they have no share in them, and He has not from them any helper"﴾ [Saba': 22].

• And His saying: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is for Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ghafir: 16];

because His saying: ﴿the One, the Subduer﴾ indicates His singularity in dominion, in subjugation, and in the entitlement to having worship sincerely devoted to Him, as is not hidden, and other verses besides that.

As for the fourth matter, namely that He, exalted is He, created everything, it has come clarified in many verses, like His saying: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth; how could He have a son when there is not for Him a companion, and He created everything, and He is, of all things, Knowing﴾ ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; there is no deity except Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him, and He is, over all things, Disposer of affairs﴾ [al-An'am: 101–102], and His saying: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things; there is no deity except Him; so how are you deluded?﴾ ﴿Thus are deluded those who used to deny the signs of Allah﴾ [Ghafir: 62–63], and other verses besides that.

As for the fifth matter, namely that He determined everything He created with precise determination, it has also come in other than this place:

• Like His saying: ﴿He who created and proportioned﴾ ﴿and who determined and then guided﴾ [al-A'la: 2–3],

• And His saying: ﴿And everything with Him is in measure﴾ [al-Ra'd: 8],

• And His saying: ﴿Indeed, all things We have created in measure﴾ [al-Qamar: 49],

and other verses besides that. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: the determination of things is their limitation by places, times, quantities, benefit, and perfection, concluded, through the transmission of Abu Hayyan in "al-Bahr".

Note.

In this noble verse there is a well-known question, which is that it may be said: "khalq" in the Arabic language means "taqdir" (determination). From it is the saying of Zuhayr:

"And you indeed measure what you create, while some of the people create and then do not measure"

Some of them said: from it is the saying of the Almighty: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 14]; he said: i.e., the best of determiners. On this basis the meaning of the verse would be ﴿and created everything﴾, i.e., determined everything, so He determined it with precise determination, and this is repetition, as you see. Al-Zamakhshari answered this question, and Abu Hayyan mentioned his answer in "al-Bahr", and did not follow it up.

The answer mentioned is his saying: "If you say that in 'khalq' there is the meaning of 'taqdir', then what is the meaning of His saying: ﴿and created everything and determined it with precise determination﴾ [al-Furqan: 2]? It is as if He said: 'and determined everything and determined it.'"

I say: the meaning is that He brought every thing into existence in a manner observing in it determination and proportion, so He determined it and prepared it for what suits it. Its example: He created man in this determined, proportioned form that you see, determining him for the duties and interests bound to him in the matters of religion and of this world. Likewise every animal and inanimate thing that came forth in a balanced, determined manner, according to the examples of wisdom and management: He determined it for a certain matter and benefit, conforming to what He determined for it, not deviating from it. Or He named God's bringing into being "creation" because He does not bring anything into being for His wisdom except in a manner of determination without disparity. So when it is said, "Allah created such-and-such," it is equivalent to your saying "He originated and brought into existence," without regard to the derivational sense; it is as if it were said: "and brought into existence every thing, determining it in its bringing into existence, not bringing it into existence disparate." It was also said: "so He made for it a term and an end," meaning: He determined it to remain until a known term. The words of the author of "al-Kashshaf" end here, and part of it has a valid direction. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 25, verse 3:

﴿Yet they have taken, besides Him, gods who create nothing, while they themselves are created, and who possess no power to harm or benefit themselves, and possess no power over death, nor life, nor resurrection.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, mentions that the gods which the polytheists worship besides Him are characterized by six things. Each one of them is a decisive proof that worshipping them alongside Allah has no justification whatsoever. Rather, it is a boundless injustice, a great ignorance, and an association (shirk) by which its practitioner will abide forever in the Fire of Hell. This comes after He praised Himself, Majestic and Exalted, with the five matters mentioned in the verse before it, which are decisive proofs that the one characterized by them is the sole deity worthy of worship. The six matters, which are attributes of the things worshipped besides Allah, are:

The first of them: that they do not create anything, i.e., they are not capable of creating anything.

The second of them: that they are all created, i.e., the Creator of everything created them.

The third: that they do not possess power to harm or benefit themselves.

The fourth, fifth and sixth: that they do not possess power over death, nor life, nor resurrection, i.e., raising after death. These six matters mentioned in this noble verse are explained in other places in the Book of Allah, the Exalted.

As for the first of them, namely that the gods worshipped besides Allah do not create anything, it is explained in many verses:

• Such as the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it﴾ [al-Hajj: 73], to the end of the verse.

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those they invoke besides Allah create nothing, and they are themselves created. [They are] dead, not alive, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾ [al-Nahl: 20–21].

• And His saying, the Exalted, in Surah "Fatir": ﴿Say: Have you considered your partners whom you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens? Or have We given them a Book so that they are upon clear evidence from it? Rather, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion﴾ [Fatir: 40]. (p-10)

• And His saying, the Exalted, in Surah "Luqman": ﴿This is the creation of Allah; so show Me what those besides Him have created. Rather, the wrongdoers are in clear error﴾ [Luqman: 11].

• And His saying, the Exalted, in "al-Ahqaf": ﴿Say: Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens? Bring me a Book before this, or a remnant of knowledge, if you are truthful﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 4].

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿I did not make them witnesses to the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor to their own creation; nor would I take misguiders as helpers﴾ [al-Kahf: 51]. Allah, the Exalted, has clarified in verses of His Book the difference between one who creates and one who does not create, because the one who creates is the one who is worshipped, and the one who does not create is not valid to be worshipped.

• Such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 21], to the end of the verse. That is: as for one who did not create you, he is not a lord, nor a deity for you, as is not hidden.

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Is then He who creates like one who does not create? Will you not remember?﴾ [al-Nahl: 17].

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or have they set up for Allah partners who created like His creation, so that the creation became confused to them? Say: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Subduer﴾ [al-Ra'd: 16]. That is: whoever is like that, then He alone is the one worshipped, Majestic and Exalted.

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Do they associate with Him that which creates nothing, while they themselves are created?﴾ [al-A'raf: 191].

As for the second matter among them, namely that the gods worshipped besides Him are created, it is explained in verses of the Book of Allah, such as the verse of "al-Nahl" and "al-A'raf" mentioned above.

As for the verse of "al-Nahl", it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those they invoke besides Allah create nothing, and they are themselves created﴾ [al-Nahl: 20]. His saying: ﴿and they are themselves created﴾ is explicit on this. As for the verse of "al-A'raf", it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Do they associate with Him that which creates nothing, while they themselves are created?﴾ [al-A'raf: 191], along with other verses.

As for the third matter among them, namely that they do not possess power to benefit or harm themselves, it is explained in several places in the Book of Allah, such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth? Say: Allah. Say: Have you then taken besides Him protectors who possess no power to benefit or harm themselves?﴾ [al-Ra'd: 16]. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Do they associate with Him that which creates nothing, while they themselves are created? And they cannot give them help, nor can they help themselves﴾ [al-A'raf: 191–192]. Whoever cannot help himself does not possess power to harm or benefit himself. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those you invoke besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves﴾ [al-A'raf: 197]. (p-11) And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is the same for you whether you call them or you remain silent. Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah are servants like you. So call upon them, and let them respond to you, if you are truthful. Do they have feet to walk with? Or do they have hands to strike with? Or do they have eyes to see with? Or do they have ears to hear with?﴾ [al-A'raf: 195–197], to the end of the verse.

In these verses is clear evidence that they do not possess anything for themselves. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if the fly should snatch away from them something, they could not retrieve it from it﴾ [al-Hajj: 73], to the end of the verse, along with other verses.

As for the fourth, fifth and sixth of the matters mentioned, namely that they do not possess power over death, nor life, nor resurrection, these too are explained in verses of the Book of Allah, such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah is He who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, then will give you life. Is there any of your partners who does any of that? Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate﴾ [al-Rum: 40].

His saying, the Exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿Is there any of your partners who does any of that? Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate﴾ clearly indicates that none of their partners is able to do any of what is mentioned in the verse, including life, which is expressed by "created you", and death, which is expressed by His saying: ﴿then will cause you to die﴾, and resurrection, which is expressed

• by His saying: ﴿then will give you life﴾. And He explained that they do not possess resurrection,

• by His saying: ﴿Or have they taken gods from the earth who raise the dead?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 21]. And He explained that they do not possess life nor resurrection, in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: Is there any of your partners who originates creation and then repeats it? Say: Allah originates creation and then repeats it﴾ [Yunus: 34], to the end of the verse. And He explained that He alone is the One in whose hand is death and life, in many verses, such as:

• His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And it is not for a soul to die except by permission of Allah, at an appointed term﴾ [Al 'Imran: 145].

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah will never delay a soul when its time has come﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 11], to the end of the verse.

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the term of Allah, when it comes, will not be delayed﴾ [Luqman: 4], to the end of the verse.

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿How do you disbelieve in Allah while you were dead and He gave you life, then He will cause you to die, then give you life again﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28], to the end of the verse.

• And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They will say: Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and gave us life twice﴾ [Ghafir: 11], to the end of the verse.

Along with other verses. What we have mentioned of the explanation of these verses by one another is known necessarily from the religion.

As for His saying, the Exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿and they possess no power to benefit or harm themselves﴾, the most evident of the opinions regarding it is that the meaning is: they do not possess power to repel harm from themselves nor to bring benefit to themselves, as al-Qurtubi and others have said. (p-12) The most that this interpretation requires is the omission of a modifying noun (mudaf) which the context indicates, and this is common in the Qur'an and in the speech of the Arabs. It has been alluded to in the "Khulasah" by his saying:

"And what follows the mudaf takes its place in its i'rab (grammatical case) when it is omitted."

It was also said that the meaning is: they are not able to harm themselves or benefit themselves with anything. The first is the more evident, meaning: if they are incapable of repelling harm from themselves and bringing benefit to themselves, then they are even more incapable regarding death, life and resurrection, because that is not something anyone can do except Allah, Majestic and Exalted.

As for His saying, the Exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿nor resurrection﴾, know that the word "nushur" (resurrection) is used in Arabic in two ways:

The first: that it is the verbal noun (masdar) of the transitive triliteral "nashara", as you say: Allah "nashara" the dead, "yanshuruhu" "nashran" and "nushuran".

The second: that it is the verbal noun of the intransitive "nashara", "al-mayyit yanshuru nushuran", with "al-mayyit" as the subject (fa'il) of "nashara".

The summary is that in the root there are three dialects. The first: "anshara-hu" in the quadriliteral form with the hamzah, "yunshiruhu" with a damma on the ya', "inshaaran". From it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then when He wills, He will raise him again﴾ [Abasa: 22], and His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And look at the bones, how We raise them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 259], with a damma on the nun and with the unpointed ra' in the recitation of Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr, and it is the present tense of "anshara-hu". The second: "nashara Allahu al-mayyit" in the form of the transitive triliteral, "yanshuru-hu", and the verbal noun in this dialect is "al-nashr" and "al-nushur". From it is His saying here: ﴿nor life, nor resurrection﴾, meaning they cannot raise anyone, with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the shin. The third: "nashara al-mayyit" in the form of the intransitive triliteral, and the meaning of "anshara-hu" and "nashara-hu" as transitive is: He gave him life after death. The meaning of "nashara al-mayyit" as intransitive is: the dead one came alive and lived after his death. The use of "al-nashr" and "al-nushur" for giving life after death, and the use of "al-nushur" for life after death, is well known in the speech of the Arabs. From their usage of "nashara al-mayyit" as intransitive, one who has come back to life is "nashir", meaning he lived after death. The saying of al-A'sha:

"If you were to lean a dead man against her chest, he would live and not be carried to the grave.
Until the people say, seeing what they saw: 'How strange, the dead man who has come back to life!'"

And from the use of "nushur" to mean giving life after death, the verbal noun of the transitive triliteral, is His saying here: (p-13) ﴿nor resurrection﴾, meaning: raising after death. And from their use of "nushur" to mean life after death, the verbal noun of the intransitive triliteral, is the saying of another:

"When you kiss her, she drinks with her mouth like the drinking of a golden-sand-coloured camel at a pool.
Then the sweetness of her caresses seizes me, with a death in my bones,
Or a languor, so we live at one time and die at another, and we mix what we die of with the resurrection."

He made the state of unconsciousness from intense pleasure a death, and recovery from it a "nushur", meaning life after death.

As for His saying, the Exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿And they have taken, besides Him, gods﴾, one of the two objects has been omitted, that is: they have taken besides Him idols as gods, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar: Do you take idols as gods?﴾ [al-An'am: 74], to the end of the verse. The word "alihah" (gods) is the plural of "ilah", and it is a pattern "fi'al" pluralized into "af'ilah", because the alif after the hamzah is substituted from a hamzah that is a silent letter and is the first radical of the word, as he said in the "Khulasah":

"And extend, change the second of the two hamzahs of a word if it is silent, as in 'a'thar' and 'a'tamin'."

And "ilah" meaning the one worshipped is of the pattern "fi'al" in the sense of "maf'ul" (passive). The use of the pattern "fi'al" in the sense of "maf'ul" has come in several examples in the Arabic language, such as "ilah" meaning "ma'luh" (the one worshipped), i.e., "ma'bud"; "kitab" meaning "maktub" (written); "libas" meaning "malbus" (worn); and "imam" meaning "ma'tamm bihi" (the one followed). It is known that the one truly worthy of worship is One, and other things worshipped are names which the disbelievers named, for which Allah sent down no authority: ﴿And those who call upon partners besides Allah do not follow except assumption, and they do nothing but guess﴾ [Yunus: 66]. ﴿They are only names you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority﴾ [al-Najm: 23], to the end of the verse.

(p-14) Concerning His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And those who disbelieved said, "This is nothing but a fabrication he has invented, and other people have helped him with it." Indeed, they have committed injustice and falsehood.﴾

In this noble verse, exalted is He, mentions that those who disbelieved and denied the Prophet ﷺ said about this Great Qur'an, which Allah revealed to him, ﴿This is nothing but a fabrication he has invented﴾. That is, this Qur'an is nothing but a lie that Muhammad ﷺ made up, and "other people helped him with it" in the fabrication he invented. It was said that these others were the Jews. It was also said that they were Addas, the freedman of Huwaytib ibn Abd al-'Uzza, and Yasar, the freedman of al-'Ala' ibn al-Hadrami, and Abu Fukayha al-Rumi. Al-Nadr ibn al-Harr al-Abdari said this.

What Allah, exalted is He, mentions in this noble verse, that the disbelievers denied him and claimed that the Qur'an is a lie that he made up, and that other people helped him in that, is explained in other verses, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves. And the disbelievers say, "This is a magician, a liar."﴾ [Sad: 4]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We substitute a verse in place of a verse, and Allah is most knowing of what He sends down, they say, "You are but a fabricator." Rather, most of them do not know.﴾ [An-Nahl: 101]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Rather, they denied the truth when it came to them, so they are in a confused matter.﴾

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But your people have denied it, while it is the truth.﴾ [Al-An'am: 66]

The verses on this are many and well known.

What Allah, exalted is He, mentions in this noble verse, that they fabricated against the Prophet ﷺ, and that other people helped him in the fabrication of the Qur'an, is also explained in other verses, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human who teaches him."﴾ [An-Nahl: 103]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So he thought and deliberated. Then he was destroyed; how he deliberated! Then he frowned and scowled. Then he turned back and was arrogant. And he said, "This is not but magic transmitted from others."﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 24] That is, Muhammad ﷺ transmits it from another. ﴿This is not but the speech of a human.﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 25]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And so that they may say, "You have studied."﴾ [Al-An'am: 105], as its explanation has already passed in Surat al-An'am. Allah, exalted is He, has denied them in this noble verse regarding what they fabricated against Him of falsehood, ﴿they have committed injustice and falsehood﴾. Al-Zamakhshari said: Their injustice is that they made the Arab learn from the non-Arab Roman a speech in Arabic that, by its eloquence, rendered all the eloquent Arabs incapable. And the falsehood (al-zur) is that they slandered him by attributing to him what he is innocent of. End of quote. Allah's denial of them in this noble verse is explained in other places in the Book of Allah, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾ [An-Nahl: 103], as its explanation has already passed in Surat an-Nahl.

• And His saying: ﴿But your people have denied it, while it is the truth.﴾ [Al-An'am: 66]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So he thought and deliberated... "This is not but magic transmitted"... "This is not but the speech of a human." I will drive him into Saqar. And what can make you know what Saqar is?﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 24-27]

Because His saying, ﴿I will drive him into Saqar﴾, after mentioning his fabrication against the Great Qur'an, indicates the greatness of his fabrication and that he will burn in the punishment of Saqar because of it. May Allah protect us, our brothers the Muslims, from it and from everything that draws near to it of speech and deed.

Know that the Arabs use jaa'a (جاء) and ataa (أتى) with the meaning of fa'ala (فعل, "did"). So His saying, ﴿they have committed (jaa'u) injustice﴾, means they did it. It was also said that a preposition is implied, meaning they came with injustice. From the use of ataa with the meaning of fa'ala is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done (bima ataw)﴾, meaning in what they did. And the words of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma:

*"Whatever good they did (ataw), it is only what their fathers' fathers inherited before them."*

Know that al-ifk (الإفك) is the worst kind of lying, because it is a turning of speech from truth to falsehood. The Arabs say afakahu (أفكه) meaning qalabahu (قلبه, "he turned it over"). From this is His saying, exalted is He, about the people of Lot: ﴿And the overturned cities (al-mu'tafikat), their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾, and His saying: ﴿And the overturned city (al-mu'tafikah), He hurled down﴾ [An-Najm: 53]. It was only called al-mu'tafikat because the Overturner (al-Malik) turned them over, that is, he overturned them, as Allah, exalted is He, made clear with His saying: ﴿We made its highest part its lowest﴾ [Hud: 82].

﴿They say: "Tales of the ancients, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening."﴾ ﴿Say: "He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth has sent it down. Indeed He is ever Forgiving, Merciful."﴾

He, exalted is He, mentioned in the first of these two verses that the disbelievers said that this Qur'an is ﴿tales of the ancients﴾, meaning that it is something the ancients wrote down and inscribed, like the stories of Rustam and Asfandiyar. They also said that the Prophet ﷺ gathered it and took it from those tales, and that he had those tales written down for himself. Al-Zamakhshari said: "That is, he wrote them down for himself and took them, as you say: istakaba al-ma' wa-istabbahu (he poured the water and had it poured for himself), when he poured it and had it poured out for himself and took it."

As for His words ﴿so they are dictated to him﴾, this means they are cast to him and recited to him when he wishes to write them down, so that he may write them. Al-Imla' (dictation) is casting speech to the scribe so that he writes it down. The hamza in it is substituted for the lam for ease, and the original form is al-imlal with a lam, as in His words: ﴿Let him who owes the debt dictate, and let him fear Allah his Lord﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-Baqarah: 282]. (The verb here is yumlali, from the root m-l-l, which in Arabic is the original form; the hamza form is a lightened variant.)

As for His words ﴿morning and evening﴾: al-bukrah means the early part of the day, and al-asil means its last part.

What He, exalted is He, mentioned in this verse, that the disbelievers said the Qur'an is tales of the ancients and that the Prophet ﷺ learned it from others and wrote it, has come clarified in several verses, such as His words: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them they say: "We have heard; if we willed, we could say the like of this. This is nothing but tales of the ancients."﴾ [al-Kahf: 31].

We have already mentioned the verses indicating that they falsely accused him of learning the Qur'an from others, and we explained their obstinacy and lying in this matter in Surat al-Nahl. The indication of the verses on that was discussed in the commentary on His words: ﴿The tongue of the one they point to is foreign﴾, so that suffices and need not be repeated here.

(p-16) Among the verses indicating their lying in His words ﴿he had it written down, so it is dictated to him﴾ is His words: ﴿And you did not recite any book before it, nor did you write it with your right hand; otherwise the falsifiers would have doubted﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 48]. Also His words: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet﴾, up to His words: ﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the unlettered Prophet﴾ [al-A'raf: 157–158]. The ummi (unlettered) is one who neither reads nor writes.

As for what He, exalted is He, mentioned in the last verse, His words ﴿Say: "He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth has sent it down"﴾ up to the end of the verse, it also comes clarified in other verses:

• Such as His words: ﴿Say: "The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord"﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-Nahl: 102].

• And His words: ﴿Say: "Whoever is an enemy to Jibril, indeed he has brought it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah"﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-Baqarah: 97].

• And His words: ﴿And indeed it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart, that you may be of the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 192–195].

• And His words: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you﴾ [Ta-Ha: 114].

• And His words: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed upon Us is its collection and its recitation. So when We have recited it, follow its recitation. Then indeed upon Us is its explanation﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 16–19].

• And His words: ﴿So I swear by what you see, and what you do not see, that indeed it is the word of a noble Messenger, and it is not the word of a poet—little do you believe—nor the word of a soothsayer—little do you remember. It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Haqqah: 38–43].

• And His words: ﴿A revelation from He who created the earth and the high heavens﴾ [Ta-Ha: 4].

And other verses besides these.

As for His words here: ﴿He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: and whoever knows the secret, there is no doubt that He knows what is openly spoken.

Among the verses indicating what this noble verse indicates, that He, exalted is He, knows the secret in the heavens and the earth, are His words: ﴿And if you speak aloud, indeed He knows the secret and what is even more hidden﴾ [Ta-Ha: 7]; His words: ﴿And keep your words secret or declare them; indeed He is Knower of what is within the breasts﴾ [al-Mulk: 13]; His words: ﴿Do they not know that Allah knows their secret and their private talk, and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 78]; His words: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private talk? Yes, and Our messengers with them are writing﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 80]; His words: ﴿That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ [al-Sajdah: 6]; His words: ﴿And know that Allah knows what is in your souls, so beware of Him. And know that Allah...﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-Baqarah: 235]; and His words: ﴿And there is not an unseen thing in the heaven or the earth but that it is in a clear Record﴾ (p-17) [al-Naml: 75]. Verses of this kind are numerous and well known.

As for His words in this noble verse: ﴿Indeed He is ever Forgiving, Merciful﴾, Ibn Kathir said about it: "It is a call to them to repentance and turning back, and an informing them that His mercy is vast, that His forbearance is great, and that whoever turns to Him, He turns to him in acceptance. Despite their lying, their fabrication, their wickedness, their slander, their disbelief, their obstinacy, and what they said about the Messenger and the Qur'an, He calls them to repentance and to abandoning what they are in, and to Islam and guidance, as He said: ﴿Certainly those who said, "Allah is the third of three," have disbelieved. But there is no god except one God. And if they do not desist from what they say, indeed a painful punishment will touch those of them who disbelieve.﴾ ﴿Will they not repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 73–74]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women and then did not repent, for them is the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the Burning﴾ [al-Buruj: 10]."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Look at this generosity and bounty! They killed His friends, and He calls them to repentance and mercy." End of the words of Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, and what he mentioned is clear.

The verses indicating the like of this are numerous, such as His words: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they desist, what has passed will be forgiven them﴾ [al-Anfal: 38], and His words: ﴿And indeed I am Most Forgiving to whoever repents, believes, and does righteous deeds﴾ up to the end of the verse [Ta-Ha: 82], and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "What is with this Messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets?"﴾. In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that the disbelievers said about our Prophet ﷺ: "What is wrong with this one who claims that he is a messenger?" This is like the saying of Pharaoh about Moses: ﴿Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is surely a madman﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 27]. That is, what is wrong with him that he eats food as we eat it, so he is in need of eating as we are in need of it, and walks in the markets, that is, because he needs to buy and sell so as to obtain his sustenance. They mean that if he were a messenger from Allah, he would be an angel of the angels, who has no need of food or of walking in the markets. The disbelievers' claim that one who eats as people eat and needs to walk in the markets to attend to his needs cannot be a messenger, and that Allah sends only an angel who has no need of food or of walking in the markets, has been made clear in many verses, and there are also verses that refute the disbelievers in this false claim of theirs.

(p-18) Among the verses that indicate their saying like what is mentioned about them in this verse is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the chiefs of his people who disbelieved and denied the meeting of the Hereafter, and whom We had given luxury in the worldly life, said, "This is none but a human being like you. He eats of what you eat and drinks of what you drink."﴾ ﴿And if you obey a human being like yourselves, then indeed you would be losers.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 33-34]. And His saying: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human being as a messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra': 94]. And His saying about them: ﴿So they said, "Shall we believe two humans like ourselves?"﴾ — the verse [al-Mu'minun: 47]. And His saying: ﴿"Shall we follow a single human being from among us?"﴾ — the verse [al-Qamar: 24]. And His saying: ﴿So they said, "Shall mere humans guide us?" And they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was self-sufficient﴾ — the verse [at-Taghabun: 6]. And His saying: ﴿They said, "You are but human beings like us, you wish to turn us away from what our fathers used to worship"﴾ [Ibrahim: 10].

Among the verses in which Allah refuted them in this false claim of theirs, and in which He explained that the messengers eat, walk in the markets, marry, and have children, and that they are of the category of human beings, except that He favoured them with His revelation and His message, and that if He had sent an angel to mankind He would have made him a man, and that if there were angels walking calmly on the earth, He would have sent down to them an angel as a messenger, because the one sent is of the same kind as those to whom he is sent, is His saying in this noble surah: ﴿And We did not send before you any messengers except that they indeed ate food and walked in the markets﴾ [al-Furqan: 20]. And His saying: ﴿And We had certainly sent messengers before you and given them wives and offspring﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 38]. And His saying: ﴿We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, from among the people of the towns﴾ [Yusuf: 109], that is, We did not make them angels, because their being men and their being from the people of the towns is explicit that they were not angels. And His saying: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man and We would have covered for them what they cover﴾ [al-An'am: 9]. Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to tell the disbelievers that he is a human being and that he is a messenger. That is because humanness does not contradict messengerhood, in His saying: ﴿Say, "Glory be to my Lord! Was I but a human being, a messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra': 93].

• And His saying: ﴿Say, "I am only a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your God is one God. So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord."﴾ [al-Kahf: 110].

• And His saying: ﴿Say, "I am only a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your God is one God, so take a straight course toward Him and seek His forgiveness"﴾ — the verse [Fussilat: 6]. And He, majestic and exalted, explained that the messengers said the like of that in His saying: ﴿Their messengers said to them, "We are only human beings like you, but Allah bestows His favour upon whom He wills of His servants"﴾ — the verse [Ibrahim: 11]. And He said: ﴿Say, "If there were in the earth angels walking calmly, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger"﴾ [al-Isra': 95]. And His saying: ﴿and walks in the markets﴾ (p-19) [al-Furqan: 7].

"Aswaq" is the plural of "suq" (market), which is feminine, though it may also be treated as masculine. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Why has an angel not been sent down to him so that he would be a warner along with him?﴾ ﴿Or a treasure be thrown down to him, or he have a garden from which he eats?﴾

Know first that "lawla" in this noble verse is, in verification, a particle of exhortation (tahdid). Tahdid is a demand made with urgency and intensity, and the author of al-Khulasah pointed to it in his saying:

"With them (lawla and lawma) is tahdid, and halla, alla, and ala; and place them before a verb."

From this you know that the present-tense verb in His saying "fa-yakuna ma'ahu nadhiran" is in the subjunctive by a concealed "an," obligatorily, because the fa' is in response to a pure demand, which is the tahdid, as he indicated in al-Khulasah with his saying:

"After fa' the answer to a negation or a demand, pure ones, 'an' is required and its concealment is obligatory in the subjunctive."

A parallel to this in the accusative with a concealed "an" after the fa' that is the answer to tahdid is His saying: ﴿So that he would say, "My Lord, why did You not delay me to a near term so I could give charity and be among the righteous"﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 10]. Because His saying "lawla akhkhartani" is a demand from him for delay, made with urgency and intensity, as the particle of tahdid, which is lawla, indicates. A parallel to it in the speech of the Arabs is the words of the poet:

"Lawla ta'uujina ya Salma 'ala danafin fa-tukhmidi nara wajdin kada yufnihi"

So His saying in the noble verse "fa-assaddaqa" is in the accusative, and the poet's "fa-tukhmidi" is also in the accusative, by dropping the nun, because the fa' is in response to a pure demand, which is the tahdid.

Know that the jussive of the verb conjoined to the accusative verb, namely His saying "wa-akun min as-salihin," is permitted only because it is a conjunction to the place (mahall); for if the fa' were dropped while intending the response of tahdid, the verb would be jussive. The permissibility of the jussive mentioned upon the mentioned dropping is what allowed conjoining the jussive to the accusative, and he indicated this in al-Khulasah with his saying:

"After other than negation the jussive is adopted, if you drop the fa' and the conditional is intended."

From what we have mentioned you know that what al-Qurtubi and others mentioned, and what az-Zamakhshari alluded to, that "lawla" in the verse is for interrogation, is not correct.

(p-20) Know that the disbelievers in this noble verse urgently and intensely proposed to him ﷺ three matters. The first: that an angel descend to him, so that he would be a warner with him, that is, to bear witness to his truthfulness and help him in conveying the message.

The second: that a treasure be thrown down to him, that is, that a treasure of wealth descend upon him from which he would spend and be independent of walking in the markets.

The third: that he have a garden from which he eats. "Janna" in the language of the Arabs means an orchard, and from it is the saying of Zuhayr:

"As if my eye, in its western corner, were a pierced water-skin of the water-wheel, watering a garden, tall (palms)."

So his saying "tasqi jannatan" means an orchard, and his saying "suhqan" means that its palm trees are tall.

These three matters mentioned in this noble verse, which the disbelievers proposed and demanded with intensity and urgency out of obstinacy and defiance, are explained in other places. Exalted is He explained in Surah Hud their proposal of the descent of a treasure and the coming of an angel with it, and that this obstinacy and defiance may constrict his chest ﷺ, in His saying: ﴿So perhaps you will leave some of what is revealed to you, and your chest will be constricted by it, lest they say, "Why has a treasure not been sent down to him or an angel not come with him?" You are only a warner﴾ [Hud: 12]. And He, majestic and exalted, explained in Surah Bani Isra'il their proposal of the garden, and made clear that by it they mean an orchard of palms and grapes, in His saying: ﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause to gush forth for us from the earth a spring"﴾ ﴿"Or you have a garden of palms and grapes and cause rivers to gush forth within it in abundance"﴾ [al-Isra': 90-91]. Their proposal here resembles Pharaoh's saying about Moses: ﴿Why have bracelets of gold not been bestowed upon him, or angels not come with him in succession?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 53]. Their hearts resembled one another, so their sayings resembled one another.

We have already put forward, in discussing the verse of Surah Bani Isra'il, these verses that indicate the abundance of the disbelievers' proposals and the intensity of their obstinacy and defiance, and that if Allah had done for them everything they proposed, they still would not have believed, as He said: ﴿And even if We had sent down to you a written scroll on paper and they touched it with their hands, those who disbelieved would have said, "This is not but obvious magic"﴾ [al-An'am: 7]. And He said: ﴿And even if We opened for them a gate from the heaven and they continued to ascend through it﴾ ﴿they would surely say, "Our eyes have only been intoxicated; rather, we are a people affected by magic"﴾ [al-Hijr: 14-15]. And He said: ﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them and We gathered against them everything in front of them, they would not have believed unless Allah willed﴾ (p-21) — the verse [al-An'am: 111]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been decreed will not believe, even if every sign should come to them﴾ — the verse [Yunus: 96-97]. And so on, among other verses, as has preceded.

Az-Zamakhshari said in his tafsir of this verse of al-Furqan: "They eat food as we eat, and move about in the markets as we move about. They mean that he should have been an angel, independent of eating and of seeking a livelihood. Then they descended from their proposal that he be an angel to the proposal that he be a human with an angel accompanying him, so that the two might help each other in warning and frightening. Then they descended again and said: If he is not supported in this way, let him be supported by a treasure thrown down to him from heaven, by which he may be strengthened and not need to seek sustenance. Then they descended once more and were content that he have a garden from which he eats and which provides for him like the landowners, or from which they themselves eat, so that they benefit from it in their worldly life and livelihood." End of quotation. All these proposals were due to the intensity of their obstinacy and defiance. The majority of the seven readers, except Hamzah and al-Kisa'i, read this letter "ya'kulu minha" with the yaa' (third person). Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "jannatun na'kulu minha" with the nun, and this reading is what az-Zamakhshari meant by his saying "or they themselves eat from that orchard."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 8:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the wrongdoers say, "You follow none but a man affected by sorcery."﴾ ﴿Look how they strike for you comparisons, so they have strayed and cannot find a way.﴾

In this noble verse, exalted and majestic is He, He mentions that the wrongdoers, namely the disbelievers, said to those who followed the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿You follow none but a man affected by sorcery.﴾ They mean that sorcery has affected him, so his intellect has been confused and his affair has become confused to him. Mujahid said: "Masḥūran" means "deceived" (makhdū'an), like His saying: ﴿Then how are you deluded?﴾ meaning, "From where are you deceived?" Some of them said: "Masḥūran" means he has a sahr, that is, a windpipe (ri'ah), so he is not independent of food and drink, and so he is a human like you, not an angel. We have already presented the words of the people of knowledge on His saying "masḥūran", with its Arabic evidence, in Surah Ta-Ha, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the sorcerer does not succeed, wherever he comes﴾ [Ta-Ha: 69]. When Allah mentioned what the disbelievers said about His Prophet ﷺ of falsehood and slander, He addressed His Prophet ﷺ with His saying: ﴿Look how they strike for you comparisons, so they have strayed and cannot find a way.﴾ What the disbelievers said in this verse, I mean their saying: ﴿You follow none but a man affected by sorcery,﴾ and what the disbelievers said in this verse, I mean His saying: ﴿Look how they strike for you comparisons,﴾ the verse, all of it has come explicitly in Surah Bani Isra'il in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿(p-22) We know best what they listen to when they listen to you, and when they are in private consultation, when the wrongdoers say, "You follow none but a man affected by sorcery."﴾ [Al-Isra': 47-48].

Al-Zamakhshari said: "They struck for you comparisons": they said about you those sayings, and they proposed for you those attributes and states that are rare, such as prophethood shared between a human and an angel, and a treasure being thrown down to you from the heaven, and other things. So they remained bewildered, astray, not finding a saying to settle upon, or they strayed from the truth, so they do not find a way to it. End of quote.

In my view, the more apparent meaning of the verse is what more than one scholar has said: that the meaning of "they struck for you comparisons" is that at times they say you are a sorcerer, at times affected by sorcery, at times a madman, at times a poet, at times a soothsayer, at times a liar. Among that is what Allah mentioned of them here: ﴿And those who disbelieved said, "This is not but a fabrication he has invented"﴾ [Al-Furqan: 4-5], and His saying: ﴿And they said, "Legends of the former peoples"﴾, and His saying: ﴿And the wrongdoers say, "You follow none but a man affected by sorcery."﴾ His saying, exalted is He: "so they have strayed" means from the path of truth, because the sayings they uttered and the comparisons they struck are all lies, fabrication and disbelief that is eternal in the Fire of Hell. Those who said them are the most astray of the astray. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so they cannot find a way﴾ has many sayings that are close to one another.

The most apparent of them is that the meaning of "so they cannot find a way" is: they cannot find a path to the truth and the right. The negation of the ability mentioned here is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They were not able to hear, nor did they see﴾ [Hud: 20], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those whose eyes were under a covering from My remembrance, and they were not able to hear﴾ [Al-Kahf: 101]. We have already presented the verses clarifying this in Surah Hud, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They were not able to hear, nor did they see﴾ [Hud: 20]. We have also already presented the meaning of injustice (zulm) and misguidance (dalal) and the various usages they carry in the language, together with the Arabic evidence, in many places in this blessed book, so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it here.

The Quranic verse ﴿Nay, they denied the Hour, and We have prepared a blazing fire for those who deny the Hour﴾. In this noble verse, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentions that the disbelievers denied the Hour, meaning they denied the Resurrection from its very foundation, because they denied being raised after death and the requital. He, Mighty and Majestic, says that He prepared and readied (*a'adda*) for those who denied the Hour, meaning who denied the Day of Resurrection, a *sa'ir*, meaning a fire of intense heat with which He will punish them on the Day of Resurrection.

(p-23) His saying, Exalted is He, in this noble verse, ﴿and We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a blazing fire﴾, indicates that denial of the Hour is a disbelief that makes one deserving of the fire of Hell, as you will soon see in the verses that show this, if Allah, Exalted, wills. These two matters mentioned in this noble verse, namely their denial of the Hour and Allah's threat of the blaze for those who deny it, have both been made clear in other verses. As for their denial of the Day of Resurrection, by denying the Resurrection (*al-ba'th*) and the requital after death, it has been mentioned in many verses concerning groups of disbelievers, such as His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, these are saying, "There is only our first death, and we will not be resurrected"﴾ [al-Dukhan: 34–35], and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78], and other verses besides these.

As for the disbelief of one who denies the Day of Resurrection and its threat of the Fire, it has come in many verses, such as His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when it was said, "Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and the Hour, there is no doubt about it," you said, "We do not know what the Hour is; we think it is only a supposition, and we are not certain"﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 32], up to His saying: ﴿And your refuge is the Fire, and you will have no helpers﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 34]. His saying, ﴿And your refuge is the Fire﴾, after His saying, ﴿you said, "We do not know what the Hour is"﴾ and so on, indicates that their saying "We do not know what the Hour is" is the cause of the Fire being their refuge. His subsequent saying, ﴿That is because you took the signs of Allah in mockery﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 35], does not contradict this, because among their taking the signs of Allah in mockery is their denial of the Hour and their denial of the Resurrection, as is clear. Also like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if you are amazed, then amazing is their saying, "When we have become dust, will we indeed be in a new creation?" Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord; those have shackles around their necks; and those are the companions of the Fire, wherein they will abide eternally﴾ [al-Ra'd: 5]. In this noble verse of Surat al-Ra'd, Allah, Exalted, has clarified that their denial of the Resurrection, which they expressed by an interrogative of denial (*istifham al-inkar*) in His saying, Exalted is He, about them, ﴿When we have become dust, will we indeed be in a new creation?﴾, combines two matters. The first of them is that it is one of the most amazing things, given the abundance of the definitive, clear proofs indicating what they denied.

The second of them, which is the point of evidence from the verse, is that their denial of the aforementioned Resurrection is a disbelief that makes them deserving of the Fire, its shackles, and abiding in it. This is in His saying, Exalted is He, referring to those who denied the Resurrection: ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord; those have shackles around their necks; and those are the companions of the Fire, wherein they will abide eternally﴾ [al-Ra'd: 5]. It is known that denying the Resurrection is denying the Hour. Also like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿(p-24) So let not one who does not believe in it [the Hour] and follows his desire divert you from it, lest you perish﴾ [Ta-Ha: 16]. That is, let not one who does not believe in the Hour divert you from believing in it, lest you perish (*fa-taradda*), meaning you be ruined because of not believing in it. *Al-Radda* is destruction, and here it means the punishment of the Fire because of denying the Hour. Allah, Exalted, has said: ﴿And his wealth will not avail him when he perishes﴾ [al-Layl: 11]. His saying, Exalted is He, in this verse of Ta-Ha, ﴿lest you perish (fa-taradda)﴾, clearly indicates that if one who does not believe in the Hour diverts you from affirming it, that will be a cause of your ruin, meaning your destruction by the punishment of the Fire, as is clear. Also like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿As for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, those will be brought forth into punishment﴾. This verse of al-Rum indicates that those who denied the meeting of the Hereafter, who are the ones who denied the Hour, are counted together with those who disbelieved and denied the signs of Allah, and that they are brought forth into punishment, which is the punishment of the Fire. Verses of this kind are numerous.

His saying, Exalted is He, in this noble verse, ﴿Nay, they denied the Hour﴾ [al-Furqan: 11]: the strongest opinion regarding it, in my view, is that it is connected to what follows it, and that *bal* in it is for transitional retraction (*al-idrab al-intiqali*), meaning a shift from one topic to another. We have explained the meaning of *sa'ir* together with some Arabic evidences at the beginning of Surat al-Hajj. And Allah, Exalted, knows best.

The Qur'anic verse on which al-Shinqīṭī comments is:

﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its raging and its roaring.﴾

In this noble verse, the Exalted and Majestic (Allah) mentions that on the Day of Resurrection, when the Fire (al-Nār) sees the disbelievers from a distant place, that is, in the open expanse of the place of gathering, its rage against those who disbelieved in its Lord intensifies and its roaring rises high. The disbelievers therefore hear its voice because of the intensity of its rage, and they hear its roaring.

What the Exalted and Majestic mentions in this noble verse is partly explained in Surat al-Mulk, where He clarifies the intensity of its rage against those who disbelieved in its Lord, and that they also hear from it a shahīq (a drawn-out, gasping sound) along with the zafīr (roaring) mentioned in this verse of al-Furqān. This is in His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿When they are cast into it, they hear from it a shahīq while it boils, almost bursting with rage﴾ [al-Mulk: 7–8]. That is, some of it nearly separates from other parts because of the intensity of its rage against those who disbelieved in Allah, Exalted is He.

The scholars have various views on the meaning of zafīr and shahīq. The closest of them is that both together are represented by the braying of a donkey: its beginning is a zafīr, and its end, which one repeats in the chest, is a shahīq.

The more apparent meaning of His saying, ﴿they hear for it raging (taghayyuẓan)﴾, is that they hear its seething because of the intensity of its rage. Since the cause of the seething is the rage, it is named by it, and this is a well-known Arabic style (uslūb). Some scholars said: "They heard for it raging" means: they perceived it, and perception includes sight and hearing; accordingly, hearing here is taken to include the sense of perception. But what we have mentioned is more apparent.

Al-Qurṭubī said: It has been said that the meaning is: when Jahannam sees them, they hear for it the sound of its rage against them. Then, at the end of his words, he stated that this view is the most correct.

* *

Issue.

Know that the verified position is that the Fire sees the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, as Allah affirmed in His saying here: ﴿when it sees them from a distant place﴾. Its seeing them from a distant place indicates the sharpness of its sight, as is clear. Likewise, the Fire speaks, as Allah affirmed in His saying: ﴿On the Day We say to Jahannam, "Are you filled?" and it says, "Are there any more?"﴾ [Qāf: 30]. The reports indicating this are many, such as the hadith of the Fire's dispute with the Garden, and the hadith of its complaint to its Lord, whereupon He permitted it two breaths, and similar reports. It suffices for this that Allah, Exalted and Majestic, has affirmed in this verse that it sees them, that it has rage against the disbelievers, and that it says: ﴿Are there any more?﴾.

Know that what many exegetes (mufassirūn) and others among those who claim to have knowledge assert, namely that the Fire does not see, does not speak, and does not rage, and that all of that is of the category of metaphor (majāz), or that it is its guardians who do these things, is entirely false and has no reliance, since it contradicts the authentic texts of revelation without any basis. The truth is what we have mentioned.

The scholars whose opinion is taken into account have agreed (ijmāʿ) that the texts of the Book and the Sunnah may not be diverted from their apparent meaning except by a proof to which one must return, as is known in its proper place.

Al-Qurṭubī said in his commentary on this noble verse: The view that the Fire sees them is the most correct. Then he said, on the basis of what has been transmitted with a raised (marfūʿ) chain that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever lies about me deliberately, let him take his seat between the two eyes of Jahannam." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, does it have two eyes?" He said: "Have you not heard Allah, Mighty and Majestic, say: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they hear for it raging and roaring﴾? A neck will come out of the Fire, having two eyes that see and a tongue that speaks, and it will say: 'I have been charged with everyone who set up another god with Allah.' It is more perceptive of them than a bird is of sesame seeds, so that it picks them up." In another narration: "A neck will come out of the Fire and snatch up the disbelievers as a bird snatches sesame seeds." Razīn mentioned this in his book, and Ibn al-ʿArabī authenticated it in his Qabas, and said: that is, it separates them from the creation in recognition, as a bird separates sesame seeds from the soil. And al-Tirmidhī narrated it from the hadith of Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection a neck will come out of the Fire, having two eyes that see and two ears that hear and a tongue that speaks, and it will say: 'I have been charged with three: with every stubborn tyrant, with everyone who called upon another god along with Allah, and with the image-makers.'" There is also a report on this from Abū Saʿīd. Abū ʿĪsā (al-Tirmidhī) said: This is a hasan gharīb ṣaḥīḥ hadith. End of the relevant point from al-Qurṭubī's words.

The author of al-Durr al-Manthūr (al-Suyūṭī) said: Al-Ṭabarānī and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the chain of Makḥūl, from Abū Umāma, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever lies about me deliberately, let him take a seat between the two eyes of Jahannam." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, does Jahannam have an eye?" He said: "Yes. Have you not heard Allah say: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place﴾? So do they see them except with two eyes?" And ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated, through the chain of Khālid ibn Duraik, from a man among the Companions, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says about me what I did not say, or claims to be the son of other than his parents, or attributes himself to other than his clients, let him take his seat between the two eyes of Jahannam." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, does it have two eyes?" He said: "Yes. Have you not heard Allah say: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place﴾?" — up to the end of his words. In it is the intensity of the terror of the Fire, and that it breathes a breath from which all creatures fear.

We ask Allah, Exalted and Majestic, to protect us and our Muslim brothers from it, and from everything that brings us near to it, whether in word or deed.

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 25, verse 13:

Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And when they are thrown into a narrow place of it, bound together, they will call out there for destruction.﴾ ﴿Do not call out today for one destruction, but call out for many destructions.﴾ In this noble verse, He mentions that when the people of the Fire are thrown, that is, cast into a narrow place of the Fire, bound together, they will call out there, that is, in that narrow place, for destruction. Then it will be said to them: ﴿Do not call out today for one destruction, but call out for many destructions.﴾ The phrase "makanan" (a place) is in the accusative as an adverb of place (ẓarf), as Abu Hayyan said in al-Bahr al-Muhit.

What He mentions here, that they are cast into a narrow place of the Fire, is also mentioned in other places, such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, it will be closed over them﴾ ﴿in extended columns﴾ [al-Humazah: 8-9], and His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved in Our signs, they are the companions of the left hand.﴾ ﴿Over them will be a closed-in Fire﴾ [al-Balad: 19-20]. The meaning of "mu'sadah" in both places, with or without the hamzah, is that its doors are sealed shut and locked upon them, as we have clarified with its Arabic evidence in Surat al-Kahf, in discussing His saying: ﴿And their dog stretches its forelegs at the threshold﴾ [al-Kahf: 18]. Whoever is in a place sealed shut and locked upon him is in a narrow place, and we seek refuge in Allah. It has been mentioned that each one of them is placed in his position in the Fire with force, just as a peg is driven into a wall. It is also reported from Ibn Mas'ud that Hell constricts upon the disbeliever like the tightening of the "zujj" (the iron ferrule at the bottom of a spear) upon the spear. The "zujj," with a damma, is the iron tip at the bottom of a spear.

As for His saying in this noble verse, "muqarranin" (bound together): it means in shackles, by the evidence of His saying in Surat Ibrahim: ﴿And you will see the criminals that Day bound together in shackles﴾ [Ibrahim: 49]. "Al-asfad" are fetters. The more apparent meaning of "muqarranin" is that the disbelievers will be bound to one another in shackles and chains. Some scholars said: every disbeliever will be bound together with his devil, and Allah has said: ﴿Until, when he comes to Us, he will say, "I wish there were between me and you the distance of the two easts; how wretched is the companion!"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 38].

This is more apparent than the view of those who said "muqarranin" means bound together by the hands, and the view of those who said it means that their hands were tied to their necks with iron collars (aghlal). "Al-thubur" means ruin, woe, and loss.

Ibn Kathir said: The more apparent view is that "al-thubur" combines loss, ruin, woe, and destruction. As Musa said to Pharaoh: ﴿And indeed, I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed﴾ [al-Isra': 102], that is, ruined. 'Abdullah ibn al-Ziba'ra al-Sahmi said:

"When one follows Satan in the paths of error,
and whoever inclines to his inclination is doomed."

End of quote.

Al-Jawhari said in his Sihah: "Al-thubur" is also ruin and loss. Al-Kumayt said:

"Qudha'ah saw, in the matter of the Yemen, the opinion of one doomed and one lost."

That is, one who is ruined and lost, meaning in her attribution to Yemen. End of quote from him.

As for His saying: ﴿They call out there for destruction﴾, the meaning of their calling for destruction is their saying: "Wa-thubura-ah!" meaning: "O woe! O destruction! Come, for this is your time and your hour."

Al-Zamakhshari said: The meaning of "And call out for many destructions" is that you have fallen into what your destruction is not one, but rather many. This is either because the punishment comes in types and kinds, each type being a destruction in its severity and horror, or because whenever their skins are roasted, they are replaced with other skins, so there is no end to their ruin. End of quote.

* *

Note.

Know that in this noble verse He said "makanan dayyiqan" (a narrow place), and likewise in al-An'am in His saying: ﴿He will make his breast narrow and constricted﴾ [al-An'am: 125], and in Hud He said: ﴿and your breast is constricted by it﴾ [Hud: 12]. What is the reason for the expression in Surat Hud, with "da'iq" on the pattern of "fa'il," while in al-Furqan and al-An'am it is "dayyiq" on the pattern of "fay'il," even though in all three places it is the descriptive form of "daqa, yadiqu," so it is "dayyiq"?

The answer to this is that it is established in the science of morphology (sarf) that all the patterns of the attributive adjective resembling the active participle (al-sifah al-mushabbahah bi-ism al-fa'il), if what is intended by them is occurrence and renewal, come on the pattern "fa'il" in every case, as Ibn Malik indicated in his Lamiyyah, saying:

"And "fa'il" is suitable for all if the occurrence is intended,
like "ghadan dha farihin jadhala" (a happy, exultant one).

If occurrence and renewal are not intended by it, it remains in its original form."

When you know this, know that His saying in Surat Hud: ﴿So perhaps you will leave some of what is revealed to you, and your breast is constricted by it﴾ [Hud: 12] means that constriction of the breast occurs to him and is renewed for him because of their obstinacy and their stubborn insistence in their saying: ﴿Why has a treasure not been sent down to him, or an angel not come with him?﴾. Since this is so, it was said about it "da'iq" in the form of the active participle. As for His saying "dayyiqan" in al-Furqan and al-An'am, it does not refer to occurrence, and therefore it remains in its original form.

From examples of the use of "fa'il" for "fa'il" when occurrence is intended is His saying: ﴿and your breast is constricted by it﴾, and the saying of Qays ibn al-Khutaym al-Ansari:

"Convey to Khidash that I am dying;
every man of noble lineage is mortal."

When he intended the occurrence of death, he said "ma'it" on the pattern "fa'il," and its original form is "mayyit" on the pattern "fay'il."

From its examples in "fa'il" (the pattern fa'iL with fatha then kasra) is the saying of Abu 'Amr Ash'ab ibn 'Amr al-Sulami, lamenting Qutaybah ibn Muslim:

"I am not one who grieves over a calamity, however great it is,
nor one who rejoices after your death."

When he negated that joy or grief would occur to him in the future, he said "jazi'" and "fari'h," and the original forms are "jazi'" and "fari'" (jaziʿ and fariḥ).

An example of it on the pattern "fa'il" (fa'ʿīl) is the saying of Labid:
