"I considered piety and generosity the best trade,
a profitable one, when a man became heavy."

When he intended the occurrence of heaviness, he said "thaqilan," and the original form is "thaqil." And the saying of al-Samhari al-'Ukli:

"In a dwelling where the miser grows fat,
while the generous people's dwelling is left desolate."

When he intended the occurrence of fatness, he said "fasamin," and the original form is "samin."

Know that the reading of Ibn Kathir, "dayqan" with a sukun on the ya' in both places, returns in meaning to the reading of the majority with the shaddah on the ya', because lightening the ya' with sukun is like "hayn" and "layn" for "hayyin" and "layyin." And Allah knows best.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Is that better, or the Garden of Eternity which the God-fearing have been promised? It will be their reward and their destination.﴾ ﴿For them therein is whatever they wish, abiding forever. It is a promise incumbent upon your Lord, one to be asked for.﴾

The verified view is that the demonstrative in His saying "Is that" refers to the Fire and the various torments the disbelievers encounter therein, as Exalted is He mentioned: ﴿And We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a blazing Fire﴾ [al-Furqan: 11], up to His saying: ﴿and you will be told, "Call today for one destruction, but call for many destructions."﴾ [al-Furqan: 14]. Other opinions are not to be relied upon, such as the view of one who said the demonstrative refers to the treasure and the garden in His saying: ﴿or he is given a treasure, or he has a garden﴾ [al-Furqan: 8], and the view of one who said it refers to the gardens and palaces made contingent upon His will in His saying: ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces﴾ [al-Furqan: 10]. The verified view, God willing, is that when He mentioned the severity and horror of the Fire's punishment, He said: "Is that torment better, or the Garden of Eternity...?"

This meaning contained in this noble verse also occurs elsewhere (p-٣٠), as in His saying in the surah "as-Saffat": ﴿Indeed, this is the great triumph.﴾ ﴿For the likes of this let the workers work.﴾ ﴿Is that better as a welcome, or the tree of Zaqqum?﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that emerges from the root of Hellfire.﴾ ﴿Its fruit is as if it were the heads of devils.﴾ ﴿Indeed, they will eat from it and fill their bellies with it.﴾ up to His saying: ﴿they will be hurried along﴾ [as-Saffat: 60–70]. And as in His saying: ﴿Is he who is thrown into the Fire better, or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ [Fussilat: 40].

There is a well-known difficulty concerning these verses and others like them in the Qur'an, namely that one may say: the word "better" (khayr) in the verses mentioned is an elative form (sighat al-tafdil), as stated in al-Kafiya:

"Often they dispense with 'better' and 'worse' in place of saying 'more good than it' and 'more evil than it'."

As I explained clearly earlier in surah an-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿For those who did good in this world there is good, and the abode of the Hereafter is better﴾ [an-Nahl: 30].

It is known in the science of Arabic grammar that the elative form requires sharing between the one preferred and the one preferred over, in respect of that in which the preference lies, except that the preferred has more of it and is superior to the one it is preferred over. It is known that the one preferred over in the mentioned verses, which is the torment of the Fire, has no good in it whatsoever. Therefore the elative form in them is problematic.

The answer to this difficulty is from two aspects. The first: the elative form may be used in the Qur'an and in the language to mean merely the attribute in general, not the preference of one thing over another. I have mentioned this many times before and cited many of its Arabic examples in surah an-Nur and elsewhere.

The second: among the methods of the Arabic language is that when they wish to single out one thing for excellence, to the exclusion of others, they use the elative form, meaning by it the exclusivity of that thing with the excellence. Such is the saying of Hassan ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him:

"Do you satirize him, when you are no match for him? So your evil is for your good: the ransom."

And as the Arabs say: "Is misery more beloved to you, or happiness?" And His saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, prison is more beloved to me"﴾ [Yusuf: 33].

(p-٣١) Abu Hayyan said in al-Bahr al-Muhit concerning His saying: ﴿Is that better...﴾ and so on: "Khayr here does not indicate preference; rather it is according to the custom of the Arabs in expressing the excellence of a thing and its being singled out for excellence to the exclusion of its opposite, as in his saying:

'So your evil is for your good: the ransom.'

And as the Arabs say: 'Is misery more beloved to you, or happiness?' And as in His saying: ﴿The prison is more beloved to me than what they call me to﴾ [Yusuf: 33]. This interrogation is by way of reproach and rebuke." End of the purpose of Abu Hayyan's words.

In any case, the torment of the Fire is pure evil with no good mixed into it whatsoever, as is evident. The two aspects mentioned in the answer are close in meaning.

As for His saying in this verse: ﴿or the Garden of Eternity which the God-fearing have been promised﴾, the returning pronoun is omitted: that is, "which the God-fearing have been promised." The verse indicates that the true promise of the Garden is attained through taqwa (God-consciousness).

We have previously presented the verses indicating this with clarity in surah an-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Thus Allah rewards the God-fearing﴾ [an-Nahl: 31].

His saying: ﴿For them therein is whatever they wish﴾ — the returning pronoun is also omitted, like the previous one: that is, "whatever they wish for." The omission of a returning pronoun in the accusative governed by a verb or a participle is common, as stated in al-Khulasa:

"Its omission among them is frequent and evident, in a connected returning pronoun if it is in the accusative,
governed by a verb or a descriptive word, like 'whom we hope, he will grant'."

This noble verse indicates that the people of the Garden find every kind of bliss they wish for.

We have previously presented the verses indicating this in surah an-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Gardens of Eden which they enter, beneath which rivers flow; for them therein is whatever they wish﴾ [an-Nahl: 31].

The verses mentioned indicate that the attainment of everything a person wishes occurs only in the Garden. His saying: ﴿They were a reward and a destination﴾ — "al-masir" is the place of arrival (as-sayrurah), and Allah has praised their reward and its place, as in His saying: ﴿How excellent a reward, and how good a resting place﴾ [al-Kahf: 31], because the goodness and excellence of a place is one of the kinds of bliss.

(p-٣٢) His saying in this noble verse: ﴿It is a promise incumbent upon your Lord, one to be asked for﴾ — there are two well-known views concerning it.

The first: the meaning of its being "asked for" is that the believers used to ask Him for it, and the angels also used to ask Him on their behalf. As for the Muslims' asking Him, Exalted is He mentioned it in His saying about them: ﴿Our Lord, give us what You promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not break the promise﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 194]. As for the angels' asking Him for them, Exalted is He also mentioned it in His saying: ﴿Our Lord, admit them to the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them﴾ [Ghafir: 47], and so on.

Some scholars said: "masy'ulan" means "obligatory," because what Allah has promised is certain to occur, since He does not break the promise, and Exalted is He obligates Himself by His true promise to whatever He wills, with no one to repel His judgment. This view is supported by the particle "upon" (ʿalā) in His saying: ﴿It is a promise incumbent upon your Lord﴾, like His saying: ﴿And it was an obligation upon Us to help the believers﴾ [ar-Rum: 47].

Some people of knowledge said: On the Day of Resurrection the Muslims will say: "We have done in the worldly abode all that You commanded us, so fulfill for us what You promised us." The first two views are closer to this. And knowledge is with Allah, Exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 17:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [mention] the Day He will gather them and what they worship other than Allah, and He will say, "Did you lead these, My servants, astray, or did they themselves stray from the way?"﴾ ﴿They will say, "Exalted are You! It was not befitting for us to take other than You as protectors. But You gave them and their fathers enjoyment until they forgot the remembrance, and they were a people ruined."﴾

The majority of the Seven Readers, except Ibn Kathir and Hafs from ʿAsim, read this letter as (naḥshuruhum) with the nun that indicates majesty, while Ibn Kathir and Hafs from ʿAsim read (yaḥshuruhum) with the yaʾ. The majority of the Seven, except Ibn ʿAmir, read (fa-yaqūlu) with the yaʾ, while Ibn ʿAmir reads (fa-naqūlu) with the nun of majesty.

The result is that Ibn Kathir and Hafs read with the yaʾ in both places, Ibn ʿAmir reads with the nun in both places, and the rest of the Seven read (naḥshuruhum) with the nun and (fa-yaqūlu) with the yaʾ. In this noble verse, exalted and high is He, has mentioned that He gathers the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, along with what they used to worship besides Him, that He will gather them all together and say to those who were worshipped: "Did you lead these, My servants, astray, by adorning for them that they should worship you besides Me, or did they themselves stray from the way?" That is: they disbelieved and associated partners with Me by worshipping you besides Me of their own accord, without you ordering them to do so or adorning it for them. The worshipped will say, "Exalted are You," that is, glorified are You above partners and everything that is not fitting to Your majesty and greatness. "It was not befitting for us to take other than You as protectors," that is: it is not for all creation, neither us nor them, to worship anyone besides You. We did not call them to that; rather they did it of their own accord, without our command, and we are free of them and of their worship. Then He said: ﴿But You gave them and their fathers enjoyment﴾ [al-Furqan: 18], that is, their lifespans were prolonged, "until they forgot the remembrance," that is, they forgot what You had sent down to them through the tongues of Your messengers, of calling to the worship of You alone, with no partner for You. "And they were a people ruined." Ibn ʿAbbas said: that is, destroyed. Al-Hasan al-Basri and Malik, from al-Zuhri, said: that is, there is no good in them. This is the purpose of Ibn Kathir's words.

Abu Hayyan said in al-Bahr: "It was not befitting for us to take other than You as protectors," that is: it would not be correct or proper for us... to the end of his words.

Now that you know what He, exalted is He, mentioned in this verse of His questioning the worshipped and their answer to Him, know that the scholars differed concerning the worshipped. Some of them said: what is meant by them is the angels, Jesus and ʿUzayr. They said: this view is supported by the Qur'an, because it contains the questioning of Jesus and the angels about the worship of those who worshipped them, as He said regarding the angels: ﴿And [mention] the Day He will gather them all, then He will say to the angels, "Did these used to worship you?"﴾ ﴿They will say, "Exalted are You! You are our protector, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them."﴾ [Saba: 40–41]. And He said regarding Jesus, upon him and upon our Prophet be prayer and peace: ﴿And when Allah says, "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah'?" He will say, "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say what I have no right to. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Your soul. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen."﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 116]. The answer of the angels and the answer of Jesus are both similar to the answer of the worshipped in this verse of al-Furqan. For this reason, more than one of the scholars chose that the worshipped whom Allah questions in this surah of al-Furqan are specifically the rational beings, excluding idols.

The one who wrote this commentary, may Allah pardon him and forgive him, says: What appears more apparent to me is that the worshipped mentioned include idols along with the angels, Jesus and ʿUzayr, because two Qur'anic indications point to this. The first: He expressed the worshipped mentioned with "mā" (what), which is used for non-rational beings, in His saying: ﴿And [mention] the Day He will gather them and what they worship other than Allah﴾, the verse. So the word (mā) indicates the inclusion of non-rational beings, and He gave precedence to the non-rational because of its abundance.

(p-34) The second indication: is the indication of verses of the Book of Allah that the worshipped are heedless of the worship of those who worshipped them, that is, they do not know of it because they are not rational, as His saying, exalted is He, in Surah Yunus: ﴿And their partners will say, "You did not used to worship us." Sufficient is Allah as witness between us and you; indeed we were unaware of your worship.﴾ [Yunus: 28–29]. They were only unaware of it because they are inanimate and do not comprehend. Applying a word specific to rational beings to them is in view of the fact that the polytheists treated them as if they were rational, as I have clarified elsewhere in this work. And like His saying in al-Ahqaf: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, one who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are heedless of their supplication?﴾ ﴿And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship.﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 5–6]. His saying, ﴿and who are heedless of their supplication﴾, indicates that they do not comprehend, and yet He said: ﴿And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship.﴾ And like His saying in al-'Ankabut: ﴿And he said, "You have taken only idols besides Allah out of affection among yourselves in this worldly life; then on the Day of Resurrection some of you will disbelieve in others and some of you will curse others"﴾, the verse [al-'Ankabut: 25]. So He explicitly stated that they are idols, then mentioned that they and their worshippers curse one another. And like His saying: ﴿No! They will deny their worship and will be opposed to them﴾ [Maryam: 82], and other verses besides these.

His saying in this noble verse, ﴿until they forgot the remembrance﴾: the apparent meaning of "forgot" (nasu) is "abandoned." The more apparent view is that "the remembrance" (al-dhikr) is what the messengers brought of monotheism. It was said: it is the remembrance of Allah by thanking Him for His blessings. The more correct view is that His saying "bur" means "ruined." Its origin is a verbal noun that applies to the singular and the plural. From its application to the plural is His saying here: ﴿and they were a people ruined﴾, and His saying in Surah al-Fath: ﴿And you thought an evil thought, and you were a people ruined﴾ [al-Fath: 12]. From its application to the singular is the saying of ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zibaʿra al-Sahmi, may Allah be pleased with him:

"O Messenger of the King, my tongue is a mender; what I have torn, I have torn while I am ruined (bur)."

"Bur" is also used to mean destruction. It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas that it is the dialect of the people of Oman, who are from the people of Yemen, and from it is the saying of the poet:

"Do not disbelieve what we have done for you, and cover it; disbelief is ruin (bur) for its doer."

Know that what al-Zamakhshari mentioned concerning this verse, and expanded upon, that Allah does not lead anyone astray, is the doctrine of the Mu'tazilah, and it is a false doctrine whose falsehood is most clear from the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ. So beware lest you be deceived by it. And what is reported from al-Hasan al-Basri and Malik, from al-Zuhri, that the meaning of "bur" is "there is no good in them," has a basis in the Arabic language, but the verification is that this is not the meaning of the verse, and that the meaning of "bur" is "ruined," as has preceded. And Allah the Exalted knows best.

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 19:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So they have indeed denied you regarding what you say﴾.

In this verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that the worshipped ones denied those who worshipped them. This is in His saying about them: ﴿They will say, "Glory be to You! It was not for us to take any protectors besides You."﴾ [al-Furqan: 18].

What this noble verse indicates regarding the worshipped ones' denial of their worshippers has come in other verses, such as:

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when mankind are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 6].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when those who associated others with Allah see their "partners," they will say, "Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to invoke besides You." But they will throw back at them the word, "Indeed, you are liars."﴾ [al-Nahl: 86].

• And His saying: ﴿So We will separate them, and their partners will say, "You did not used to worship us."﴾ [Yunus: 28].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿No! They will deny their worship of them and will be opponents to them﴾ [Maryam: 82].

Verses similar to these are many and well known.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever wrongs among you, We will make him taste a great punishment﴾. Ibn Kathir said: "Whoever wrongs among you," i.e., associates others with Allah. Al-Qurtubi also mentioned this from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. This interpretation is supported by verses from the Book of Allah, such as:

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is the disbelievers who are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 254].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not invoke other than Allah that which neither benefits you nor harms you, for if you do, then indeed you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ [Yunus: 106].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is a great injustice﴾ [Luqman: 13]. It is also established in Sahih al-Bukhari that the Prophet (ﷺ) explained the wrongdoing (ẓulm) in His saying: ﴿Those who believed and did not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾ [al-An'am: 82], and said: i.e., with shirk (associating partners with Allah), as we have previously explained in detail.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 20:**

Allah's words: ﴿And We have made some of you a trial for others﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, mentions that He has made some people a trial (fitnah) for others.

The meaning indicated by the verse is also mentioned in His words: ﴿And thus We have tried some of them by means of others, that they might say, "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?"﴾ [Al-An'am: 53], and so on.

[p. 36] Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (commentary) of His words, ﴿And We have made some of you a trial for others﴾: The meaning of this is that each one of you is tested by his companion. The wealthy person is tested by the poor person: he must help him and not mock him. The poor person is tested by the wealthy person: he must not envy him, nor take from him except what he gives him, and each of them must be patient upon the truth. This is as al-Dahhak said regarding the meaning of ﴿Will you be patient?﴾ [Al-Furqan: 20]: that is, upon the truth. Those who suffer afflictions say, "Why were we not spared?" The blind man says, "Why was I not made like the one who sees?" And so it is with the possessor of every calamity. The Messenger, who was specifically honoured with the dignity of prophethood, is a trial for the nobles of the disbelievers in his era. Likewise the scholars and the rulers of justice. Do you not see their saying: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from the two cities?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 31]? So the trial is that the afflicted envies the healthy, and the healthy belittles the afflicted; and patience is that each of them restrains himself: the former from insolence (batar), and the latter from impatience (dajar). The essential point of al-Qurtubi's words ends here.

When you have understood the meaning of some of them being a trial for others, know that His words, ﴿And thus We have tried some of them by means of others﴾ [Al-An'am: 53], contain the trial of the wealthy disbelievers by the poor believers, in that they belittled them and looked down upon them, and denied that Allah would bestow His favour upon them rather than upon themselves, because in their opinion, due to their poverty and the shabbiness of their condition, Allah could not possibly show them mercy and give them of His abundant bounty. This is as Allah said, relating about them that they said concerning them: ﴿Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 11], and He said: ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us?﴾ [Sad: 8], and other verses to this effect. Allah will rebuke them on the Day of Resurrection for their belittling of them in the world, as He said: ﴿Are these the ones of whom you swore that Allah would never grant them mercy? Enter Paradise; no fear will be upon you, nor will you grieve﴾ [Al-A'raf: 49]. And His words: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks﴾ … up to His words: ﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, upon couches, looking on. Have the disbelievers been recompensed for what they used to do?﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin: 29–36]. And His words: ﴿And those who disbelieved mock those who believed, while those who feared Allah will be above them on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 212]. And His words: (Will you be patient?), that is, upon the truth, or will you not be patient? And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

(p. 37) In this noble verse, the Most High mentions that those who do not hope for the meeting with God said: ﴿Why were the angels not sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?﴾ Here, *lawla* (why not) is *lil-tahḍīḍ* (expressing urging or exhortation).

The meaning is that they demanded, with urgency and vehemence, that the angels be sent down upon them, or that they see their Lord. This arrogant demand that God mentions here, namely their request for the angels to be sent down to them or for them to see their Lord, He mentions in another place, as in His saying: ﴿Or you bring God and the angels before us as a guarantee﴾ [al-Isra' 17:92], and their saying: ﴿Why were the angels not sent down to us?﴾ It has been said: "Then let it be revealed to us as it was revealed to you." This view is supported by His saying: ﴿They say: "We will not believe until we are given the like of what was given to the messengers of God"﴾ [al-An'am 6:124] and the rest of the verse. It has also been said: "Why were the angels not sent down to us so that we could see them directly?" This view is supported by His saying: ﴿Or you bring God and the angels before us as a guarantee﴾ [al-Isra' 17:92], meaning, face to face, according to this view. We have already presented the opinions on this in Surat Bani Isra'il.

As for His saying in this noble verse, ﴿who do not hope (*la yarjūna*)﴾, some scholars said: "*La yarjūna* means they do not fear the meeting with Us, because they do not believe in the Resurrection." The word *al-rajā'* (hope) is used for fear just as it is used for desire. Some scholars said: Among its uses is His saying: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not expect dignity from God?﴾ [Nuh 71:13], meaning, you do not fear the greatness of God. And among its uses is the saying of Abu Dhu'ayb al-Hudhali:

*When the bees sting him, he does not expect their sting,*
*and he keeps away from them in a honeycomb hive of honey.*

His saying "he does not expect their sting" means he does not fear their sting. Some people of knowledge said: using *al-rajā'* for fear is the dialect of Tihama. Some scholars said: ﴿who do not hope for Our meeting﴾ means they do not aspire to it. This was attributed to al-Qurtubi, who cited it from Ibn Shajara, and said: Among its uses is the saying of the poet:

*Does a people who killed Husayn hope*
*for the intercession of his grandfather on the Day of Reckoning?*

meaning: Does a people who killed Husayn aspire to... etc. One who does not believe in the Resurrection does not fear meeting God, because he does not believe in punishment, and he does not hope for good from Him, because he does not believe in reward.

As for His saying, Most High: ﴿They have become arrogant within themselves﴾, it means they concealed arrogance toward the truth in their hearts and held it as a belief, out of obstinacy and disbelief. This meaning is clarified by His saying: ﴿There is nothing in their breasts but pride, which they will never attain﴾ [Ghafir 40:56]. And His saying: ﴿And they have acted with great insolence﴾, meaning they transgressed the limit in wrongdoing and rebellion. It is said: "So-and-so acted insolently toward us," meaning he exceeded the limit in wronging us. His describing their aforementioned insolence as being accompanied by pride indicates that they went to excess in it, and that they reached the utmost degree of arrogance and the farthest extent of insolence. This noble verse indicates that the denial of the messengers after the evidence of the miracles, the clarity of the truth, their obstinacy, and their demanding, by requesting the sending down of angels or seeing God, is a great arrogance toward the truth and a great insolence, which deserves that its bearer receive punishment and reproach. Therefore God intensified His rebuke against whoever was so obstinate and arrogant in refusing to accept the truth, as in His saying: ﴿Or do you wish to question your Messenger as Moses was questioned before?﴾ [al-Baqara 2:108]

• And His saying: ﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a book from heaven. They asked Moses for something greater than that, saying: "Show us God openly," so the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:153].

• And His saying: ﴿And when you said: "O Moses, we will never believe you until we see God openly," the thunderbolt seized you while you were looking on﴾ [al-Baqara 2:55].

The Mu'tazila (a rationalist theological school) use this verse and similar ones as evidence that seeing God is impossible. Their argument is false, and their doctrine, God forbid, is among the greatest misguidance and the most profound falsehood. The statement of al-Zamakhshari in his commentary on this verse, that God cannot be seen, is a false statement and corrupt speech.

The truth beyond doubt is that the believers will see God with their eyes on the Day of Resurrection, as the hadiths have been transmitted in successive chains from the truthful and trusted one (ﷺ), and the Qur'anic verses indicate it both explicitly and implicitly, as we have clarified in another place.

We have already presented in this surah and in Surat Bani Isra'il the verses indicating that even if God had done for them everything they proposed, they would not have believed. That suffices, so we do not repeat it here.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On the Day they see the angels, there will be no good tidings that Day for the guilty, and they will say, "A forbidding, forbidden barrier."﴾ In this noble verse, He, may He be majestic and exalted, mentions that the disbelievers who demanded that angels be sent down to them: on the Day they see the angels, there will be no good tidings for them, meaning their seeing the angels will not gladden them, and at that time it will not be good news of anything good for them. Their seeing the angels occurs at the time of their death (ihtidar), and it occurs on the Day of Resurrection, and there will be no good tidings for them in seeing them in either of the two times.

As for their seeing the angels at the arrival of death, verses from the Book of Allah have indicated that there is no good tidings for them in it, because of the punishment they encounter from the angels at death.

As in His saying, may He be exalted: (p-39) ﴿If only you could see when the angels take the lives of those who disbelieve, striking their faces and their backs﴾ [al-Anfal: 50], up to the end of the verse.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If only you could see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death, and the angels are stretching out their hands, [saying], "Release your souls. Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth and what you used to be arrogant toward of His signs."﴾ [al-An'am: 93]

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So how will it be when the angels take them, striking their faces and their backs? That is because they followed what angered Allah and disliked His pleasure, so He nullified their deeds.﴾ [Muhammad: 27–28]

As for their seeing the angels on the Day of Resurrection, there is also no good tidings for them in it. What indicates this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and then they would not be reprieved.﴾ [al-An'am: 8]

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿there will be no good tidings that Day for the guilty﴾ [al-Furqan: 22] indicates by the evidence of its address (dalil al-khitab), i.e., the implication of its opposite (mafhum al-mukhalafa, the meaning understood by contrast), that for those who are not guilty, on the Day they see the angels, there will be good tidings. This implication from this verse has been stated explicitly in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised. We are your allies in the worldly life and in the Hereafter, and for you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you ask for. As a hospitable gift from the Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful."﴾ [Fussilat: 30–32]

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿and they will say, "A forbidding, forbidden barrier."﴾ In my view, the stronger of the two opinions regarding it is that it is part of the speech of the disbelievers on the day they see the angels, not part of the speech of the angels. Its clarification: the disbelievers who had demanded the sending down of angels, when they saw the angels, expected punishment from them, so they would then say to the angels: "A forbidding, forbidden barrier," meaning: it is prohibited and forbidden for you to touch us with harm, because we have not committed a sin that would make us deserving of punishment. This is as He, may He be exalted, made clear in His saying about them: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves. Then they will offer submission, [saying], "We did not do any evil." Yes, indeed Allah is Knowing of what you used to do.﴾ [al-Nahl: 28]. Their saying, ﴿We did not do any evil﴾, means: we did not deserve punishment, so punishing us is forbidden and prohibited. Allah refuted their claim with His saying: ﴿Yes, indeed Allah is Knowing of what you used to do.﴾ It is the custom of the Arabs, in whose language the Qur'an was revealed, that they say this expression, i.e., "A forbidding, forbidden barrier," when meeting an enemy seeking vengeance, or upon the sudden onset of a calamity, or the like.

Sibawayh has mentioned this expression, I mean "ḥijran maḥjūran," in the chapter on non-inflecting verbal nouns (al-maṣādir ghayr al-mutaṣarrifa) which are put in the accusative by verbs whose appearance is omitted, such as: "Ma'adha Allah" (I seek Allah's refuge) and "'Amraka Allah" (by your life, by Allah), and the like.

(p-40) His saying, "ḥijran maḥjūran": its origin is from ḥajarahu, meaning "he prevented him." And ḥijr means "the forbidden," because it is prohibited. From it is His saying: ﴿And they say, "These are livestock and tilth, forbidden (ḥijr); none may eat of them except whom we wish," by their claim.﴾ [al-An'am: 138], i.e., forbidden. From it is also the saying of al-Mutalammis:

"She longed for the farthest palm, so I said to her: a forbidden barrier, are those not the ... (al-dahārīs)?"

Here, "ḥarām" (forbidden) is an emphasis of "ḥijr," because its meaning is "forbidden." And the saying of another:

"Has not Asmā' become a forbidden barrier, and has she not become, of her in-laws' closest kin, a father-in-law?"

And the saying of another:

"She said, while in her was bewilderment and terror: 'I seek refuge in my Lord from you, and a barrier.'"

His saying "maḥjūran" is an emphasis of the meaning of ḥijr. Al-Zamakhshari said: like the Arabs' saying: "dhayl dhā'il" (a humiliating humiliation) and "mawt māʾit" (a dying death). As for the view that "ḥijran maḥjūran" is part of the speech of the angels, its meaning is that they say to the disbelievers: "ḥijran maḥjūran," i.e., forbidden and prohibited that there should be good tidings for the disbelievers today, or that they should be forgiven, or that they should enter Paradise. This view was chosen by Ibn Jarir, Ibn Kathir, and others.

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿On the Day they see the angels﴾. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Yawm" (the Day) is in the accusative by one of two things: either by what is indicated by "lā bushrā" (no good tidings), i.e., on the Day they see the angels they will be prevented from good tidings or deprived of them, and "yawma'idhin" is for emphasis; or by the implied "udhkur" (mention), i.e., mention the Day they see the angels, then He said: there will be no good tidings that Day for the guilty.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 23:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust.﴾ We have already presented the verses clarifying this in several places in this blessed Book: in Surah al-Isra' (Banu Isra'il), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the effort due to it while he is a believer﴾ [al-Isra' 19], and in Surah al-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer﴾ [al-Nahl 97], and elsewhere. That has sufficed in place of repeating it here.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 24:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode and a finer resting place.﴾

Some scholars have derived from this noble verse that the reckoning of the people of Paradise is easy and that it ends at midday. The basis for this is that His saying "maqilan" (a resting place), i.e., a place of qaylulah (the midday rest), and qaylulah is resting at midday. They said: what is understood from this noble verse has its explanation in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will be called to a easy account. And he will return to his people in joy.﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 7-9].

It is understood from His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse, ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode﴾ and so on, that the companions of the Fire are not like that, and that their reckoning is not easy.

This understanding is indicated by other verses, such as His saying, exalted is He, near to this verse: ﴿The sovereignty on that Day belongs to the Most Merciful, and it will be a difficult Day for the disbelievers.﴾ [al-Furqan: 26]. His saying "for the disbelievers" indicates that it is not difficult for the believers, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾ and so on [al-Anbiya: 103]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Hastening toward the caller. The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."﴾ [al-Qamar: 8]. When you know from what we have mentioned the verses that clarify His saying: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode and a finer resting place﴾, these are the sayings of some exegetes regarding the meaning we have mentioned in the verse.

The author of al-Durr al-Manthur said: Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿a better abode and a finer resting place﴾, that he said: "In the chambers of Paradise. Their reckoning will be that they are presented before their Lord in a single presentation, and that is the easy reckoning, like His saying: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will be called to an easy account. And he will return to his people in joy.﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 7-9]." Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, related from Ibn Mas'ud. He said: "The day of Resurrection will not reach midday until these and those rest," then he recited: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode and a finer resting place﴾, and he recited: "Then indeed their resting place is toward the Hellfire." Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "It is only a forenoon. The friends of Allah will rest on couches with the wide-eyed houris, and the enemies of Allah will rest with the devils, bound together."

Ibn al-Mubarak, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu Nu'aym in (p-٤٢) al-Hilyah related from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i: "They used to hold that the reckoning of people on the Day of Resurrection will be completed at midday. The people of Paradise will rest in Paradise, and the people of the Fire in the Fire. That is His saying: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode and a finer resting place﴾."

Ibn Jarir related from Sa'id ibn al-Saffar who said: "It has reached me that the Day of Resurrection will be shortened for the believer, until it is like the period between the afternoon prayer and sunset, and they will rest in the gardens of Paradise when people have finished the reckoning, and that is His saying: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode and a finer resting place﴾," and so on. Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ikrimah who said: "I truly know the hour in which the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire: it is the hour when the great forenoon rises, when people return to their families for the midday rest. The people of the Fire will go to the Fire, while the people of Paradise will be taken to Paradise, and their midday rest will be in Paradise, and they will be fed the liver of the fish, which satisfies them all. That is His saying: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode and a finer resting place﴾."

al-Qurtubi mentioned something similar, attributing it to the Prophet ﷺ, and said: "al-Mahdawi mentioned it. The apparent view is that it is not authentic as a marfu' report." al-Qurtubi also said: "Qasim ibn Asbagh related from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, regarding ﴿a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 4], 'I said: How long this day is! He ﷺ said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, it will be made light for the believer until it is lighter for him than the obligatory prayer.'" And this is also weak. As for what he related from Ibn Mas'ud, that he recited "Then indeed their resting place is toward the Hellfire," it is known that this is an irregular reading (shadhdh) with which recitation is not permissible, and the true recitation is ﴿Then indeed their return is toward the Hellfire﴾ [al-Saffat: 68].

Know that the saying of Qatadah regarding this verse is well-known and famous, and according to it there is no evidence in the verse for what we have mentioned. Qatadah's saying is that the meaning of His saying "a finer resting place" is a dwelling and a place of refuge, and this interpretation has no evidence in it for the midday rest, as you see.

We have shown in our book (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab) the way of reconciling what this verse indicates, namely the conclusion of the reckoning at midday, with what His saying indicates: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾. We mentioned the verses that point to the reconciliation and some Arabic evidence.

Know that the well-known usage in the speech of the Arabs is that al-maqil means the qaylulah or its place, which is resting at midday during the heat, for example, even if sleep does not accompany it. From it is the saying:

"May Allah reward the best of people with the best of His rewards, the two companions who stopped at the tents of Umm Ma'bad."

That is, they stopped there at the time of qa'ilah, as stated by the author of Lisan al-'Arab. And what Qatadah explained the verse by, that al-maqil is the dwelling and the abode, is also known in Arabic speech. From it is the saying of Ibn Rawahah:

"Today we strike you for His revelation, a blow that removes the skull from its maqil."

His saying "removes the skull from its maqil" means it removes the heads from their places on the necks, and it is known that the maqil there is the place where the heads rest. And it is apparent that of this kind is the saying of Uhayhah ibn al-Julah al-Ansari:

"You do not know, even if you resolve a matter, in which land the maqil will overtake you."

According to this, the meaning is: in which land the reward and abiding will overtake you through death or other causes. The form of comparison in His saying here, "a better abode and a finer resting place," we have discussed something similar shortly before, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Say: Is that better, or the Garden of Eternity?﴾ and so on [al-Furqan: 15].

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-٣٥٦) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Furqan.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode and a finer resting place.﴾

This noble verse indicates that the reckoning concludes at midday, because al-maqil is for qaylulah or its place, which is the rest at midday in the heat.

Among those who said that the reckoning concludes at midday were Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, Ikrimah and Ibn Jubayr, relying on this verse for that, as Ibn Kathir and others related from them.

In Tafsir al-Jalalayn is the text: "It is derived from this that the reckoning concludes at midday, as is related in a hadith," end quote. Yet He, exalted is He, mentioned that the measure of the Day of Resurrection is fifty thousand years in His saying: ﴿in a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 4].

The apparent answer is that the Day of Resurrection is long for the disbelievers and short for the believers. This is pointed to by His saying, exalted is He, a little after this: ﴿The sovereignty on that Day belongs to the Most Merciful, and it will be a difficult Day for the disbelievers﴾ [al-Furqan: 26]. So His restricting the difficulty of that Day to the disbelievers indicates that the believers are not like that. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So that Day will be a difficult Day, for the disbelievers, not easy﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 9-10] also indicates by its implication that it is easy for the believers, not difficult.

As also indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Hastening toward the caller. The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."﴾ [al-Qamar: 8]. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus related to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed us that Sa'id al-Saffar related to him that it reached him that the Day of Resurrection will be shortened for the believers until it is like the period between the afternoon and sunset, and that they will turn over in the gardens of Paradise until people are finished, and that is His saying: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode and a finer resting place﴾. Ibn Kathir related it from him in his tafsir. It is known that joy makes time seem short, while sorrows and worries cause it to be long, as Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith said, lamenting the Prophet ﷺ [al-Wafir]:

"I was kept awake, so my night stayed and does not pass, and the night of the one afflicted by calamity is long within it."

Another said:

"Their short ones with sorrows are long, and their long ones with joy are short."

And the one who said it excelled:

"My night and Layla's night, their difference banished my sleep, in length; and length would be my happiness if the two were balanced.

My night gives length generously whenever Layla is stingy with length, and if she gives it generously, it is stingy."

Such usage is very common in the speech of the Arabs. As for the view of those who explain al-maqil as the dwelling and the abode, like Qatadah, may Allah have mercy on him, there is no contradiction at all between the two verses, because the meaning according to this view is: the companions of the Garden on that Day have a better abode and a finer dwelling and place, and Allah knows best.

The Words of Allah Most High: ﴿And [mention] the Day the heaven will be split open with the clouds, and the angels will be sent down, descending [in procession]﴾. In this noble verse, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, mentions that the heaven will be split open on the Day of Resurrection with the clouds, and that the angels will be sent down in a descent. Al-Qurtubi said: "The heaven is split open with the clouds," i.e., "from the clouds." He said: "The preposition bi (with) and ʿan (from) are interchangeable, as in your saying: rumiytu bi-l-qaws (I was shot with the bow) and ʿan al-qaws (from the bow)." End of quotation. The meaning of ʿan is supported by the words of Allah Most High: ﴿On the Day the earth will split asunder from them, hastening [forth]﴾ [Qaf: 44], to the end of the verse.

These three matters mentioned in this noble verse, namely the splitting of the heaven on the Day of Resurrection, the presence of the clouds, and the descent of the angels, are all clarified in other places in the Qur'an.

As for the splitting of the heaven on the Day of Resurrection, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, has explained it in many verses of His Book, such as:

• His Words: ﴿And when the heaven is split open and becomes rose-colored like red leather﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 37].

• His Words: ﴿So on that Day the Inevitable Event will occur. And the heaven will be split open, for it that Day will be frail﴾ [Al-Haqqah: 15–16].

• His Words: ﴿When the heaven splits open﴾ [Al-Inshiqaq: 1], to the end of the verse.

• His Words: ﴿And when the stars are obliterated. And when the heaven is opened﴾ [Al-Mursalat: 8–9], to the end of the verse. His words "furijat" mean "shuqqat" (were split), so there will be in it furuj, i.e., cracks.

• As in His Words: ﴿When the heaven breaks apart﴾ [Al-Infitar: 1].

• And His Words: ﴿And the heaven will be opened and will have gates﴾ [An-Naba: 19].

As for the clouds and the descent of the angels, Allah Most High mentioned them together in His Words: ﴿Do they await only that Allah should come to them within canopies of clouds, and the angels [also]?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 210], to the end of the verse. Allah, Majestic and Exalted, has mentioned the descent of the angels in other verses, such as:

• His Words: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank﴾ [Al-Fajr: 22].

• His Words: ﴿Do they await only that the angels should come to them, or your Lord should come, or some of the signs of your Lord…﴾ [Al-An'am: 158], to the end of the verse.

• His Words: ﴿We do not send down the angels except with truth, and they would then not be reprieved﴾ [Al-Hijr: 8].

Az-Zamakhshari said: The meaning is that the heaven will be opened with a cloud that comes out of it, and within the cloud the angels will descend, and in their hands will be the scrolls of the deeds of the servants. End of quotation from him.

This word was read by Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Ibn ʿAmir as "tashsharaqqa" (تَشَّقَّقَ) with the shadda on the shin, while the rest read it with the letter lightened by omitting one of the two tas. Ibn Kathir read "wa-nunzilu al-malaikata" (ونُنْزِلُ الملائكة) with two nuns, the first one dammed and the second one sukun, with the zay lightened and the lam dammed, as the present tense of anzala (to send down), with al-malaikata in the accusative as the direct object. The rest read it with one nun and a shadda-ed, kasra-ed zay, as a past passive verb, with al-malaikatu in the nominative as the deputy subject of nuzzila. The more apparent view is that yawma (the Day) is in the accusative, governed by an implied udhkur (mention), as al-Qurtubi said. And Allah knows best.

The Exalted said in this noble verse: ﴿The dominion on that Day belongs truly to the Most Merciful, and it will be a difficult Day for the disbelievers.﴾

In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentioned two matters: that true dominion on the Day of Resurrection belongs to Him alone, to the exclusion of any other, and that the Day of Resurrection will be difficult for the disbelievers.

These two matters mentioned in this noble verse have been clarified in other verses of the Book of Allah. As for the dominion belonging to Him on the Day of Resurrection, He, exalted be He, mentioned it in several verses of His Book:

• such as the saying of He, majestic and exalted: ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Fatihah: 4]

• and His saying: ﴿Whose is the dominion this Day? It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ghafir: 16]

• and His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And His is the dominion on the Day when the Horn is blown﴾ [al-An'am: 73]

along with other verses besides these.

(p-45) As for the Day of Resurrection being difficult for the disbelievers, we have already presented the verses that indicate it shortly before, in the discussion of His saying, exalted be He: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will be better in resting place﴾, and so on.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And on the Day when the wrongdoer bites his hands, saying, "Oh, would that I had taken a way with the Messenger!"﴾ ﴿"Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a close friend!"﴾ ﴿"He led me astray from the Reminder after it had come to me. And Satan is ever a deserter of man."﴾

Among the well-known points of the scholars of tafsir (exegesis) is that the wrongdoer concerning whom this verse was revealed is ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt, and that the "so-and-so" who led him astray from the Reminder was Umayyah ibn Khalaf, or his brother Ubayy ibn Khalaf. Some scholars have mentioned that in the recitation (qira'ah) of some of the Companions there is: "Would that I had not taken Ubayy as a close friend." Even if this is established, it is on the level of tafsir (explanation) and not of recitation (qira'ah). In any case, what counts is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the occasion of revelation. So every wrongdoer who obeyed his close friend in disbelief, until he died upon that, will be treated in the same way as Ibn Abi Muʿayt was treated.

What Allah, may He be exalted, mentions in these noble verses is clarified in other passages. His saying ﴿And on the Day when the wrongdoer bites his hands﴾ is a kinayah (allusive expression) for intense regret and anguish, because one who regrets intensely bites his hands. The regret and anguish of the disbeliever on the Day of Resurrection, which this verse indicates, is clarified in other verses, such as:

- His saying, may He be exalted, in Surat Yunus: ﴿And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment, and it will be judged between them with justice﴾ [Yunus: 54], and so on.
- His saying, may He be exalted, in Surat Saba': ﴿And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment, and We will place shackles upon the necks of those who disbelieved﴾ [Saba': 33], and so on.
- His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They will say, "Oh, our grief over what we neglected concerning it!"﴾ [al-An'am: 31]. Al-hasrah (grief) is the most intense form of regret.
- His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Thus Allah will show them their deeds as regrets upon them, and they will not be removed from the Fire﴾ [al-Baqarah: 167], and other verses.

As for what is mentioned here, that the disbeliever wishes he had believed in the Messenger in the life of this world and had taken a way with him, i.e., a path to Paradise, in His saying here: ﴿"Oh, would that I had taken a way with the Messenger!"﴾, this is clarified in other verses, such as:

- His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On the Day when their faces are turned over in the Fire, they will say, "Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger!"﴾ [al-Ahzab: 66]
- His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He will say, "Oh, would that I had sent forth for my life!"﴾ [al-Fajr: 24]
- His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims﴾ [al-Hijr: 2], and other verses.

The "way" (sabil) which the disbeliever wishes he had taken with the Messenger, mentioned in this verse, is also mentioned in other verses, such as:

- His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble surah, Surat al-Furqan: ﴿Say, "I do not ask you for any reward for it, except that whoever wills may take a way to his Lord"﴾ [al-Furqan: 57].
- His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills may take a way to his Lord﴾ [al-Insan: 29 and 33; and in al-Muzzammil: 19], and close in meaning is the return (ma'ab) mentioned in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That is the true Day; so whoever wills may take to his Lord a return﴾ [al-Naba': 39].

As for what is mentioned here, that the disbeliever calls out "woe" and wishes that he had not taken as a close friend the one who misled him, it is mentioned in other places than this. As for the disbelievers' calling out "woe," it has already been mentioned in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when they are thrown into a narrow place therein, bound together, they will call out there for destruction. "Do not call out today for one destruction, but call out for many destructions"﴾ [al-Furqan: 13-14]. As for their wish not to have obeyed those who misled them, it is also mentioned in other places than this, such as:

- His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who followed will say, "If only we had another return, so we could disassociate ourselves from them as they have disassociated themselves from us"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 176]. The particle law (lau) in His saying ﴿If only we had another return﴾ is for wishing (tamanni), and for this reason the imperfect verb after the fa' in His saying ﴿so we could disassociate﴾ is in the subjunctive mood. This is clear evidence of their regret over their allegiance to them and their obedience to them in the world.

As for what Allah, may He be exalted, mentions here, that the companions of misguidance, from the devils of mankind and jinn, lead their companions astray from the Reminder after it has come to them, it is mentioned in other places than this, such as:

- His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And their brothers extend them in error, then they do not restrain﴾ [al-A'raf: 202].
- His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We appointed for them companions who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them﴾ [Fussilat: 25], and so on.
- His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the Day He gathers them all, "O assembly of jinn, you have taken much from mankind"﴾ [al-An'am: 128], and so on.
- His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they will say, "Our Lord, we obeyed our leaders and our elders, and they led us astray from the way"﴾ [al-Ahzab: 67].
- His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Until, when they have all gathered therein, the last of them will say of the first of them, "Our Lord, these led us astray, so give them a double punishment of the Fire"﴾ [al-A'raf: 38].
- His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If only you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, returning word to one another. Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Were it not for you, we would have been believers"﴾ [Saba': 31], and other verses.

His saying, may He be exalted, here: ﴿And Satan is ever a deserter of man﴾. The more apparent view is that this is from the speech of Allah, and not from the speech of the regretful disbeliever on the Day of Resurrection. Khadhul (deserter) is an intensive form (sighah mubalaghah). The Arabs say, "khadhalahu" when he abandons his support while expecting support from him. From this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if He forsakes you, who is there that can support you after Him?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 160].

The saying of the poet:

"Indeed, a man dies not merely at the ending of his life,
but he dies when he is wronged and then deserted."

And the saying of another:

"Indeed, those who described my people to them,
by them, hold fast; you will meet whoever opposes you deserted."

Among the verses that show that Satan deserts man is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Satan said when the matter was concluded, "Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I broke it to you. And I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I disbelieve in what you associated with Him before﴾ [Ibrahim: 22]. And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when Satan made their deeds attractive to them and said, "No one among mankind can overcome you today, and indeed I am your protector." But when the two groups sighted each other, he turned back on his heels and said, "Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see"﴾ [al-Anfal: 48], and other verses.

His saying, may He be exalted, in this verse: ﴿He led me astray from the Reminder﴾. The more apparent view is that the Reminder is the Qur'an. His saying ﴿so-and-so﴾: the Arabs use the word "fulan" as a kinayah (allusive expression) for a man of unknown or unnamed identity, i.e., "I did not take Ubayy or Umayyah as a close friend." They use "fulanah" as a kinayah for a woman. From this is the saying of ʿUrwah ibn Hizam al-ʿUdhri:

"Ah, may Allah fight the slanderers and their saying:
'So-and-so has become a beloved of so-and-so.'"

His saying ﴿The wrongdoer bites﴾: from ʿaDiDa with a kasrah on the ʿayn in the past tense, and it is yaʿaDDu with a fathah on the ʿayn in the present, according to the analogy. From this is the saying of al-Harith ibn ʿAlqah al-Dhahli:

"Now that my temple has turned white,
and I bit upon a stump from my tooth..."

The well-known narration of the line is ʿaDiDtu with a kasrah on the first dad, and there is a dialect with a fathah on the ʿayn in the past tense, but the kasrah is more well-known. ʿaDDa is transitive with ʿalā, as in the verse and in the line of al-Harith ibn ʿAlqah mentioned. It may also be transitive with the bāʾ, from which is the saying of Ibn Abi Rabiʿah:

"She said, and bit with her fingertips, 'You have disgraced me,
while you are a man whose affair is easy, and yours is difficult.'"

This noble verse indicates that an evil companion may bring his companion into the Fire. Warning against the evil companion is well-known and established. In Surat al-Saffat, Allah, may He be exalted, has explained that a man from the people of Paradise swore by Allah that his companion had nearly ruined him, i.e., destroyed him with the punishment of the Fire. But Allah was gentle with him, and His mercy and favor overtook him, so He guided him and saved him from the Fire. This is in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿A speaker among them said, "Indeed, I had a companion"﴾ ﴿who would say, "Are you among those who believe?"﴾ ... to His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So he looked and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire﴾ ﴿He said, "By Allah, you nearly ruined me!"﴾ ﴿"And if not for the favor of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forth."﴾ [al-Saffat: 51-57].

The Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 25, verse 30:

God Almighty says: ﴿And the Messenger says, "O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned."﴾

The meaning of this noble verse is clear: our Prophet (ﷺ) complained to his Lord about the abandonment of his people, the disbelieving Quraysh, of this Great Qur'an. That is, they left it, not believing in it and not acting upon it. This is a great complaint, and in it is the greatest warning to whoever abandons this Great Qur'an, so that he does not act upon what it contains of lawful and unlawful, of manners and noble qualities, and does not hold to the creedal beliefs it contains, and does not take a lesson from its warnings, stories and parables.

Know that al-Subki (Taj al-Din al-Subki) said that he derived from this noble verse, in Surah al-Furqan, a legal-theoretical issue (mas'alah usuliyyah, a question of the principles of jurisprudence), namely that refraining from an act is an act. By "refraining" is meant leaving something undone. He said in his Tabaqat (the Tabaqat al-Shafi'iyyah al-Kubra): "I have come upon three proofs which indicate that refraining is an act. I have not seen anyone discover them."

The first: God's words: ﴿And the Messenger says, "O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned."﴾ For the verb "taking" (al-akhdh) means receiving, and "abandoned" (mahjur) means left. So the meaning becomes: they received it as something left, that is, they performed its abandonment. The point of the matter has concluded through the transmission of the author of Nashr al-Bunud, Sharh Maraqi al-Su'ud (an explanatory commentary on the poem Maraqi al-Su'ud, on the principles of jurisprudence), in his discussion of the line:

"So our refraining from forbidding is the Prophet's sought-for demand."

The compiler of this work, may God pardon him and forgive him, says: al-Subki's deduction from this verse, that refraining is an act, and his explanation of it in a way that indicates this, did not appear to me fully clear. However, this meaning which he claimed this noble verse indicates, namely that refraining is an act, is indicated by two noble verses of Surah al-Ma'idah, clearly, without ambiguity or dispute. So, supposing the correctness of what al-Subki understood from this verse of al-Furqan, the two mentioned verses of al-Ma'idah have explained it with clarity.

As for the first of them, it is God's words: ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them from their sinful speech and their consumption of the unlawful? Evil indeed is what they used to do.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 63]. So the rabbis' and scholars' abandonment of forbidding them from sinful speech and from consuming the unlawful, God, Mighty and Majestic, called in this noble verse "doing" (sun') in His words: ﴿Evil indeed is what they used to do﴾, that is, their abandonment of the mentioned forbidding. And "doing" (sun') is more specific than the general term "act" (fi'l). So the clarity of this noble verse's indication that abandonment is an act is in the utmost clarity, as you see.

As for the second verse, it is God's words: ﴿They did not forbid one another from any wrong they committed. Evil indeed is what they used to do.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 79]. God, Mighty and Majestic, in this noble verse called their abandonment of forbidding wrong an "act," and He established blame for it with the word "evil" (bi'sa), which is a rigid verb used to express blame, in His words: ﴿Evil indeed is what they used to do﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 97]. That is, their abandonment of forbidding every wrong they committed. The clarity of this verse's indication of what has been mentioned is also clear, as you see.

Prophetic hadiths also indicate this, such as his (ﷺ) saying: "A Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe." In this hadith he (ﷺ) called abandoning harm to Muslims "Islam." Among what indicates from the speech of the Arabs that abandonment is an act is the saying of some of the Companions at the time of the Prophet's (ﷺ) building of his mosque in Medina:

"If we sit while the Prophet is working, that would indeed be a misguided work."

So he called their sitting idle from work, and their leaving it, a misguided work. The author of Maraqi al-Su'ud pointed out that refraining is an act according to the (correct) school of thought, that is, the truth. He explained branches of law built upon this, which Shaykh al-Zaqqaq versified in his poem called al-Manhaj al-Muntakhab (The Chosen Method). He cited al-Zaqqaq's verses on this and said: "I have brought them here by way of incorporation (tadmin), and this type is called isti'anah (borrowing), which is incorporating one verse or more into one's own words with the line:"

"So our refraining from forbidding is the Prophet's sought-for demand, and refraining is an act in the sound school of thought."

"It has branches mentioned in al-Manhaj, and listing them comes after this verse:"

"From giving drink, or thread, the zakat of surplus, and of pillars, the writing of testimony, and such"

"Whoever leaves idle, and the one holding a pledge likewise, and the one negligent in providing fodder, so derive the principle."

"And like the wife returned for a defect, and her guardian's lack, and similar matters known."

The last three verses are from the versification of Shaykh al-Zaqqaq called al-Manhaj al-Muntakhab, and they contain some branches built on the disagreement about refraining: is it an act, which is the truth, or not? Al-Zaqqaq's words in the first of his verses, "from giving drink," are connected to the line before it:

"And is one who refrains like one who acts? He has the capacity for benefit, but he is like one who..."

"...from giving drink," etc.

(p. 50) So his words "from giving drink" explain the benefit implied in the line: "He has the capacity for benefit, but he is like one who," that is, he left off the benefit while being able to provide it. His leaving it is like his doing it, for what results from his leaving it of harm, according to the view that abandonment is an act. His meaning with "from giving drink" is that whoever has a surplus of drink and withholds it from a person in dire need until he dies of thirst: according to the view that abandonment is an act, he is liable for the blood money; according to the view that it is not an act, there is no liability on him. The surplus of food is like the surplus of drink in this. His words "or thread" mean that whoever withholds thread he has from someone whose belly is split open, or who has a penetrating wound, until he dies, is liable for the blood money according to the view that abandonment is an act, and according to the opposite view there is no liability. His words "zakat" mean that whoever passes by game whose death-wound has not been completed and who is able to slaughter it, but does not slaughter it until it dies, is he liable for it or not? This is according to the disagreement mentioned.

His words "the surplus of" mean that whoever has water in excess of what he needs for irrigating his crops, while his neighbour has crops and no water, if he withholds the water from him until his crops perish, is he liable or not? This is according to the disagreement mentioned. His words "and pillars" mean that if he has pillars (plural of 'amud, a column), and he withholds them from a neighbour whose wall is in danger of collapse, until it collapses, is he liable or not? His words "the writing of testimony" mean that whoever withholds a document containing testimony to a right until the right is lost, is he liable or not? His words "and whoever leaves idle" mean that the guardian over an orphan's property, for example, if he leaves its house unrented, so that the benefit of renting it is lost for a period, or leaves the land until it becomes barren, is he liable or not? His words "and the one holding a pledge" mean that if the pledgee (mortgagee) leaves the pledge unrented, so that the benefit from it is lost for a period, and its rent was of importance to him, is he liable or not? His words "likewise, the one negligent in providing fodder" mean that whoever leaves an animal with someone, with its fodder, and says to him: "Put the fodder before it," and he leaves off putting it before it until it dies, is he liable or not? "Fodder" in the verse is with a sukun on the second letter, and it means the act of putting fodder before it, with a fatha on the second letter.

His words:

"And like the wife returned for a defect, and her guardian's lack"

mean: if the nearest guardian marries off his ward, and there is a defect in her that justifies annulling the marriage, and the wife remains silent and does not disclose her own defect, and the guardian is insolvent, does the husband recover the dowry from the wife or not? These branches and what resembles them are built on the disagreement over refraining: is it an act or not? The correct view is that refraining is an act, as the Book, the Sunnah and the language indicate, as has been explained previously. Accordingly, the correct view is that liability is required in the matters mentioned.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 31:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals. And sufficient is your Lord as guide and helper.﴾

When the Prophet (ﷺ) complained to his Lord in His saying: ﴿And the Messenger says, "O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned."﴾, Allah sent down His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy﴾ [al-Furqan: 31], as consolation for him (ﷺ). That is: just as We made the disbelievers enemies to you, denying you and taking the Qur'an that was revealed to you as something abandoned, so too is this appointing: ﴿We have appointed for every prophet an enemy﴾, that is, We have appointed for you enemies, just as We appointed for every prophet an enemy.

As for His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy﴾ [the verse], we have already presented its explanation in "al-An'am", in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy: devils of mankind﴾ [the verse] [al-An'am: 112]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And sufficient is your Lord as guide and helper.﴾ We have already presented a full discussion of "kafa" (sufficed), both intransitive and transitive, with its Arabic evidences, in surah "al-Isra'", in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as accountant﴾ [al-Isra': 14] [sic: 41 in the source reference]. As for His saying: ﴿And sufficient is your Lord as guide﴾, its meaning has come clarified in many verses, such as His saying: ﴿Whomever Allah guides, he is the one guided﴾ [al-Isra': 97], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the guidance"﴾ [al-An'am: 71]. And His saying: ﴿and helper﴾, that is, and sufficient is your Lord as helper; its meaning has also come in many verses, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If Allah helps you, no one can overcome you; but if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 160].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 32:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thus, that We may strengthen your heart thereby, and We have recited it in measured recitation.﴾

The verses with a similar meaning have already been discussed at the end of Surat al-Isra', in the commentary on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And a Qur'an We have divided, that you might recite it to the people over a long period. And We have sent it down in stages﴾ [al-Isra': 106], and His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿Thus, that We may strengthen your heart thereby﴾. That is: thus is the revelation sent down in parts, according to events; We sent it down in parts and not all at once, as they proposed. His saying, ﴿that We may strengthen your heart thereby﴾, means: We sent it down in parts so that We might strengthen your heart by sending it down in parts.

Some scholars said: its meaning is that by revealing it in parts, We strengthen your heart to memorize it, because memorizing it piece by piece is easier than memorizing it all at once, had it been sent down in one go.

Some scholars also said: What confirms this is that he, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, was unlettered (ummi), who could neither read nor write.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 34:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who will be gathered on their faces to Hell — those are worse in position and further astray from the way.﴾

In this noble verse, exalted and majestic is He, mentioned that the disbelievers will be gathered on their faces to Hell on the Day of Resurrection, and that they are worse in position and further astray from the way. He explained in other places that their faces will be overturned in the Fire and that they will be dragged on their faces within it:

• As in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed, their faces will be overturned into the Fire﴾ [an-Naml: 90]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day their faces are turned over in the Fire﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Ahzab: 66]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces, "Taste the touch of Saqar."﴾ [al-Qamar: 48]

And exalted and majestic is He explained in Surat Bani Isra'il that they will be gathered on their faces, and He added to that that they will be gathered blind, mute and deaf. And in Surat Ta-Ha He mentioned that the disbeliever will be gathered blind. He said in Surat Bani Isra'il: ﴿And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces, blind, mute and deaf; their refuge is Hell. Whenever it subsides, We increase for them the blaze.﴾ [al-Isra': 97] And He said in Surat Ta-Ha: ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed for him is a constricted life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind.﴾ ﴿He will say, "My Lord, why have You gathered me blind, while I was [once] seeing?"﴾ ﴿He will say, "Thus came to you Our verses, but you forgot them."﴾ to the end of the verse [Ta-Ha: 124–126].

We have already explained the manner of reconciling the verse of Bani Isra'il and the verse of Ta-Ha mentioned, together with the verses indicating that the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection will see, speak and hear:

• As in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How clearly they will hear and see on the Day they come to Us﴾ [Maryam: 38]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us that we may do righteousness; indeed, we are certain﴾ [as-Sajdah: 12]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire and will be certain that they are going to fall into it﴾ [al-Kahf: 53]

In Surat Ta-Ha, in the discussion of His saying, ﴿And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾. Likewise, we explained the aspects of reconciliation among the verses mentioned in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab", in the discussion of the mentioned verse of Bani Isra'il.

As for the comparative form in His saying, ﴿Those are worse in position and further astray from the way﴾, we have previously discussed the like of it in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Is that better, or the Garden of Eternity which the righteous have been promised?﴾ [al-Furqan: 15]. And "makan" (place, position) is the locus of existence. Apparently it is both sensory and figurative. The sensory is evident; the figurative is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "If he steals, a brother of his had stolen before." So Joseph concealed it within himself and did not reveal it to them. He said, "You are worse in position"﴾ to the end of the verse [Yusuf: 77]. And "al-sabil" (the way, path) may be masculine or feminine, as previously mentioned. From its masculine usage is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they see the way of guidance, they will not take it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will take it as a way﴾ [al-A'raf: 146]. And from its feminine usage is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight"﴾ to the end of the verse [Yusuf: 108].

(p-53) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book and made his brother Aaron with him a minister﴾ ﴿So We said, "Go to the people who denied Our signs," and We destroyed them with complete destruction﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this matter in the surah of "Maryam" (Mary), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We called him from the right side of the mount and brought him near as a confidant﴾ [Maryam: 52].

Allah's statement: ﴿And the people of Noah, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them and made them a sign for mankind﴾. We have already mentioned some of the verses that indicate the manner of their drowning in Surah "al-A'raf," in the discussion of His statement: ﴿And We drowned those who denied Our signs﴾ [al-A'raf: 64].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And ʿAd and Thamud and the companions of the Rass, and many generations between them.﴾ In my view, the more apparent reading is that His saying "ʿAdan and Thamuda" is conjoined (ma'tuf) to His saying "and the people of Nuh," and that "the people of Nuh" is the direct object (maf'ul bihi) of a verb omitted (mahdhufah) for "We drowned," which is indicated by His saying after it: ﴿We drowned them and made them a sign for the people﴾, in accordance with the rule stated in his (Ibn Malik's) "al-Khulasah":

"The preceding noun is put in the accusative by a verb that is necessarily hidden, which agrees with what has been mentioned."

That is: We destroyed the people of Nuh by drowning, and We destroyed ʿAd, Thamud and the companions of the Rass, and many generations between that, i.e., We destroyed many generations between that mentioned, namely the people of Nuh, ʿAd and Thamud.

The more apparent view is that the many generations mentioned after the people of Nuh, ʿAd and Thamud, and before the companions of the Rass. A verse from Surah Ibrahim has indicated that after ʿAd and Thamud there were peoples who disbelieved and denied the messengers, and that no one knows them except Allah, exalted is He.

His explicit statement that they were after ʿAd and Thamud clarifies what we have mentioned, and that is in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Has there not come to you the report of those before you: the people of Nuh, and ʿAd and Thamud, and those after them, whom none knows except Allah?
