Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they put their hands over their mouths and said: "Indeed we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, and indeed we are in grave doubt about that to which you invite us."﴾ [Ibrahim: 9].

We have already presented the words of the scholars on the meaning of His saying: ﴿they put their hands over their mouths﴾. The reference in His saying "between that" returns to ʿAd, Thamud and the companions of the Rass, i.e., between that mentioned.

The return of a demonstrative or a pronoun in the singular to multiple referents, based on what has been mentioned, is a well-known Arabic idiom. Among its instances with the demonstrative is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said: "Indeed He says it is a cow neither old nor virgin, but between that"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 68], i.e., that mentioned, of the old and the virgin. And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He is between that, a moderate course﴾ [al-Furqan: 67], i.e., between that mentioned, of extravagance and stinginess. And the saying of ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zaba'ra al-Sahmi:

"Indeed for good and for evil there is an end, and both of that are a direction and a destination."

i.e., both of that mentioned, of good and evil. And among its instances with the pronoun is the saying of Ru'bah:

"In it are lines of black and white, as if on the skin is the spreading of leprosy."

i.e., "as if it," meaning what was mentioned of the lines of black and white. We have already presented this verse.

As for ʿAd and Thamud, the story of each of them has come in detail in several verses. As for the companions of the Rass, the details of their story have not come in the Qur'an, nor the name of their prophet. The exegetes have many sayings about them, which we have left aside because none of them has any evidence.

Al-Rass, in the language of the Arabs, is the well that is not lined (with stone). Al-Jawhari said in his "Sihah" that it is the well lined with stones. Among its application to a well is the poet's saying:

"They are travelling toward their land, so would that they were digging the wells (al-rissas)."

And the saying of al-Nabighah al-Ja'di:

"I outran to a company of drinkers, Tanabilah, digging the wells (al-rissas)."

Al-Rissas in the two verses is the plural of rass, which is the well. Al-Rass is also a valley, in the saying of Zuhayr in his Mu'allaqah:

"They set out at dawn and entered the dawn-time, so they are for the valley of al-Rass like the hand to the mouth."

His saying in this verse: ﴿and generations between that, many﴾ is the plural of qarn, which here means the generation of people who were contemporaneous in existence in some period of time.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 39:**

The Exalted said, ﴿And to each We struck examples, and to each We utterly destroyed with complete destruction.﴾ In this noble verse, He, may He be majestic and exalted, mentions that each of the bygone destroyed peoples, from the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, the People of the Rass (Ashab al-Rass), and the many generations between them, was given examples (amthal) by Him, so that He might make the truth clear to them through the striking of examples. This is because the intelligible becomes like the perceptible through an example. He also mentions that He, may He be majestic and exalted, destroyed all of them with tatbir, that is, He annihilated them all with a total destruction that uprooted them. The word al-tatbir (تَتْبِيرًا) means destruction and breaking. From its usage is the Exalted's saying, ﴿And that they might destroy what they had overcome with complete destruction﴾ [al-Isra': 7]. Also His saying, ﴿Indeed, these people are doomed (mutabbar) in what they are engaged in﴾ [al-A'raf: 139], meaning, false. And His saying, ﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers except in ruin (tabar)﴾ [Nuh: 28], meaning, destruction. These two matters mentioned in this noble verse, namely that He, may He be majestic and exalted, struck examples for each of them, and that He destroyed them all with complete destruction, have both been mentioned in other places.

As for His striking of examples for the disbelievers, He, may He be majestic and exalted, mentioned it in other places, such as His saying in Surat Ibrahim: ﴿Had you not sworn before that there would be for you no decline? And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We struck for you examples﴾ [Ibrahim: 44-45]. As for His destruction of all the nations for denying their messengers, it has come clarified in many verses, such as His saying in Surat al-A'raf: ﴿And We did not send into any town a prophet except that We seized its people with adversity and hardship that they might humble themselves. Then We replaced evil with good until they multiplied [in prosperity] and said, "Adversity and ease have touched our forefathers," so We seized them suddenly while they were unaware﴾ [al-A'raf: 94-95]. And His saying in Surat Saba': ﴿And We did not send into any town a warner except that its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with"﴾ [Saba': 34]. And His saying in al-Zukhruf: ﴿And thus We did not send before you into any town a warner except that its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we found our forefathers upon a religion, and indeed, we are following in their footsteps"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 23]. And His saying: ﴿Then We sent Our messengers in succession. Every time a nation's messenger came to them, they denied him, so We caused them to follow one another, and We made them into tales﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 44], up to the end of the verse, and other verses indicating that all nations denied their messengers, and that Allah destroyed them because of that. He, may He be majestic and exalted, has explained in another verse that this generality did not exclude anyone except the people of Yunus, and not others. That is in His saying: ﴿So why was there not a town that believed and its faith benefited it, except the people of Yunus? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and let them enjoy for a time﴾ [Yunus: 98].

Also indicating this is His saying: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more. And they believed, so We let them enjoy for a time﴾ [al-Saffat: 147-148]. As for what He, may He be majestic and exalted, mentioned in this noble verse, that He struck examples for each of them, it does not clarify here whether He also struck examples for this noble nation, which is the last of the nations in this Qur'an, as He struck them for other nations. However, He, may He be exalted, has clarified in many verses that He (p-56) struck examples for this nation in this great Qur'an, so that they might reflect upon them, and He explained that none understands them except those of knowledge, and that Allah guides by them some people and misguides by them others.

Among the verses indicating all of this is His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example, even of a mosquito or what is above it. As for those who believed, they know that it is the truth from their Lord; but as for those who disbelieved, they say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?" He misleads thereby many and guides thereby many, and He misleads thereby none except the defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Baqarah: 26]. And His saying: ﴿And We have certainly struck for mankind in this Qur'an from every kind of example that perhaps they may remember﴾ [al-Zumar: 27]. And His saying: ﴿And these examples We present to the people, that perhaps they will give thought﴾ [al-Hashr: 21]. And His saying: ﴿And these examples We present to the people, but none will understand them except the knowledgeable﴾ [al-Ankabut: 43]. And His saying: ﴿O mankind, an example has been presented, so listen to it﴾ [al-Hajj: 73], up to the end of the verse. The verses indicating this are many and well known, and knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they have certainly passed by the town upon which was rained a rain of evil. Have they not been seeing it? Rather, they have not been expecting resurrection.﴾

In this verse, exalted is He swears that the disbelievers who denied our Prophet (ﷺ) have indeed passed by the town upon which was rained a rain of evil, namely that Allah rained upon it stones of sijjil, and it is Sodom, the town of the people of Lut. The two matters mentioned in this noble verse, namely that Allah rained upon this town a rain of evil, which is the stones of sijjil, and that the disbelievers passed by it, are made clear in other verses.

As for Allah raining the said stones upon it, exalted is He mentioned this in many verses, such as His saying: ﴿So We made its highest part its lowest and rained upon them stones of sijjil﴾ [al-Hijr: 74]. In surah "al-Dhariyat" He made clear that the sijjil mentioned is a kind of clay, in His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have been sent to a people who are criminals, to send upon them stones of clay﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 32-33]. There is no doubt that this clay is painful in its impact, severe and destructive. And His saying: ﴿And We rained upon them a rain, and evil was the rain of those who were warned﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 173], and His saying: ﴿By your life, indeed they were wandering in their intoxication. So the Cry seized them at sunrise. So We made its highest part its lowest and rained upon them stones of sijjil﴾ [al-Hijr: 72-74], and so on.

As for their having passed by that mentioned town, this too is made clear in other places, such as His saying: ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning, and at night. Will you not then reason?﴾ [al-Saffat: 137-138]. What is meant is that they passed by the town of the people of Lut, and their passing by it and seeing it empty of its people, with no caller and no responder in it, because Allah destroyed all its people for their disbelief and their denial of His messenger Lut. In this is the greatest admonition and the most mighty deterrent against denying our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), lest there befall those who denied him the like of what befell the people of Lut of punishment and destruction. By this He rebuked them for not taking heed of what punishment had been sent down upon it. This is like His saying in the aforementioned verse of "al-Saffat": "Will you not reason?" And like His saying in this verse of "al-Furqan": ﴿Have they not been seeing it? Rather, they have not been expecting resurrection﴾. So His saying: ﴿Have they not been seeing it?﴾ is a rebuke for them for not taking heed, like His saying in the other verse: "Will you not reason?" It is known that they pass by it in the morning and at night, and that they see it. And like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We rained upon them stones of sijjil. Indeed in that are signs for those who discern. And indeed it is on an established road﴾ [al-Hijr: 74-76]. He means that the dwellings of the people of Lut are on an established road, i.e., an established path, which they pass by on their journeys to al-Sham.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Rather, they have not been expecting resurrection﴾, i.e., they do not fear a raising or a recompense, or they do not expect a raising or a reward.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 41:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when they see you, they take you not except in mockery: "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?"﴾ ﴿"He nearly led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast in adhering to them."﴾ Its clarification has already passed in Surat al-Anbiya' (the Chapter of the Prophets), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you not except in mockery: "Is this the one who mentions your gods?" while they, at the mention of the Most Merciful, are disbelievers.﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 36]. As for what they said here, that they were steadfast regarding their gods, it is made clear in Surat Sad that some of them commanded others to it, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the eminent ones among them went forth, saying: "Walk on, and be steadfast in adhering to your gods."﴾ and so on, the verse [Sad: 6].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 43:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have you seen one who takes as his god his own desire? Would you then be a guardian over him?﴾ Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his tafsir of this verse: ﴿Have you seen one who takes as his god his own desire﴾, meaning: whatever he finds pleasing of a thing and sees as good according to his own desire becomes his religion and his way, until he said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "A man in the Jahiliyyah would worship a white stone for a time, and when he saw something better than it, he would worship the second and abandon the first." End of quote from him.

(p-58) The author of "al-Durr al-Manthur" mentioned that Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that the unbeliever's worship of the second stone in place of the first is the occasion of revelation of this verse. Then the author of "al-Durr al-Manthur" said: Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi, who said: "In the Jahiliyyah they would eat blood mixed with al-'ilhiz (a kind of plant-based stuff), and they would worship a stone. When they found something better than it, they would throw it away and worship the other. When they lost the other, they would order a herald, who would call out: 'O people, your god has gone astray, so seek him!' So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿Have you seen one who takes as his god his own desire﴾." Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿Have you seen one who takes as his god his own desire﴾, that he said: "That unbeliever took his religion without guidance from Allah or any proof."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Hasan concerning: ﴿Have you seen one who takes as his god his own desire﴾, that he said: "He does not desire anything except that he follows it."

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Qatadah: ﴿Have you seen one who takes as his god his own desire﴾, he said: "Whenever he desires something he mounts it, and whenever he craves something he goes to it, and no restraint or piety holds him back from that."

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated from al-Hasan that he was asked: "Is there shirk among the people of the qiblah?" He said: "Yes. The hypocrite is a polytheist. The polytheist prostrates to the sun and the moon besides Allah, and the hypocrite worships his desire." Then he recited this verse: ﴿Have you seen one who takes as his god his own desire? Would you then be a guardian over him?﴾

Al-Tabarani narrated from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Under the shadow of the sky there is no god worshipped besides Allah that is greater in the sight of Allah than a followed desire." End of the relevant point from the words of the author of "al-Durr al-Manthur."

The clarification of the scholars' statements mentioned concerning this verse is that the obligation that must be acted upon is that all the actions of the mukallaf (responsible person) conform to what his Worshipped One, may He be majestic and exalted, has commanded him. So when all his actions follow what he desires, he has directed all the worship and obedience that his Creator is owed toward his desire. Therefore, that he has taken his desire as his god is most clear.

Once you know this meaning which this noble verse indicates, know that Allah, may He be majestic and exalted, explained it in another place, in His saying: ﴿Have you seen one who takes as his god his own desire, and Allah has led him astray knowingly, and has sealed over his hearing and his heart, and placed a covering over his sight? Who then will guide him after Allah?﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 23], (p-59) and His saying: ﴿Is one to whom the evil of his deed is made attractive so that he sees it as good [equal to one who does not]? For indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾ [Fatir: 8].

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿Would you then be a guardian over him?﴾, it is a rhetorical question of denial which carries the meaning of negation.

The meaning: that whoever Allah has led astray and who has taken his desire as his god, you are not a guardian over him, i.e., a protector who guides him and turns away from him the misguidance that Allah has decreed upon him; because guidance is in the hand of Allah alone, not in your hand, and what is incumbent upon you is only the conveying (of the message), and you have conveyed it.

This meaning which this noble verse indicates has come clarified in many verses, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Qasas: 56].

• His saying: ﴿If you are eager for their guidance, indeed Allah does not guide one who leads himself astray﴾ [al-Nahl: 37].

• His saying: ﴿Is one upon whom the word of punishment has come [to be saved]? Would you then save one who is in the Fire?﴾ [al-Zumar: 19].

• His saying: ﴿Would you then compel the people until they become believers? And it is not for a soul to believe except by the permission of Allah﴾ [Yunus: 99–100].

• His saying in the aforementioned verse of Fatir: ﴿For indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, so let not yourself go in pursuit of them through regret﴾ [Fatir: 8].

• His saying in the aforementioned verse of al-Jathiyah also: ﴿So who will guide him after Allah?﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 23].

The verses similar to these are many, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 44:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do you suppose that most of them hear or understand? They are only like livestock; rather, they are further astray in way.﴾ As for ﴿أم﴾ (am) in this noble verse, it is the disjunctive (munqati'ah) one, and its most well-known meaning is that it combines the meaning of ﴿بل﴾ (bal, "rather"), which signals a turn away (idrab), with the interrogative of denunciation (istifham al-inkar) together. The turn signified by it here is a transitional turn (idrab intiqali).

The meaning is: "Rather, do you suppose that most of them hear or understand?" That is: do not believe that or think it. For they do not hear the truth nor understand it, that is, they do not grasp it with their minds. ﴿They are only like livestock﴾, that is: they are nothing but like livestock, which are camels, cattle and sheep, in not hearing the truth and not perceiving it. ﴿Rather, they are further astray than livestock﴾, that is: further removed from understanding the truth and perceiving it.

As for His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse, ﴿Rather, they are further astray in way﴾, al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, how were they made more astray than livestock?

I say: Because livestock submit to their owners who feed and look after them; they recognize who treats them well from who mistreats them; they seek what benefits them and avoid what harms them; and they find their way to their pastures and watering places. These people do not submit to their Lord, nor do they recognize His kindness toward them, following the enticement of Satan who is their enemy; they do not seek the reward, which is the greatest benefit; they do not guard against the punishment, which is the greatest harm and ruin; and they are not guided to the truth, which is the wholesome law and the sweet, pure water. End of quotation from him.

Now that you know what this noble verse indicates, know that Allah has explained it in other places, such as His saying in Surah al-A'raf: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. They are like livestock; rather, they are further astray. Those are the heedless.﴾ [al-A'raf: 179], and His saying in al-Baqarah: ﴿The example of those who disbelieve is like one who shouts to that which hears nothing but a call and cry. Deaf, dumb, and blind, so they do not reason.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 171].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 47:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who made for you the night as a garment, and sleep a rest, and made the day a resurrection﴾. In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that it is He who made the night a garment for His creation, and sleep a rest (subat), and made the day for them a resurrection (nushur). As for His making the night a garment for them, the apparent meaning is that when He made the night cover all who are on the earth with its darkness, it became a garment for them, concealing them as a garment conceals the nakedness of its wearer. Perhaps they benefit from the garment of the night, such as the escape of a Muslim captive from the disbelievers in the darkness of the night, and his being concealed by it until he is saved from them, and other benefits that are obtained because of the garment of the night, as Abu al-Tayyib al-Mutanabbi said:

"How often has the darkness of night done me a favour that proves the Manichaeans are liars."

"It protected you from the enemies' harm as you travelled toward them, and the one of veiled beauty visited you in it."

As for His making sleep a rest (subat), most of the exegetes hold that what is meant by subat is rest from the fatigue of work during the day, because sleep cuts off daytime work, so fatigue ends with it and rest is attained, as is well known.

Al-Jawhari said in his "Sihah": "Subat is sleep, and its origin is rest, and from it is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And We made your sleep a rest﴾ [An-Naba: 9]." Al-Zamakhshari said in his "Kashshaf": "Subat is death, and the masbut is the dead, because he is cut off from life, and this is like His saying: ﴿And it is He who takes you back at night﴾."

If you say: Why not explain it as rest? I say: the word nushur in opposition to it refuses that, refusing as a camel-shy of the water-drink refuses, when it is turbid. End of the relevant point from him.

The clarification of his words is that nushur is life after death, as its explanation has already preceded. Accordingly, His saying ﴿and made the day a resurrection﴾ means life after death. On this basis, death is what is expressed by subat in His saying ﴿and sleep a subat﴾, and the application of death to sleep is well known in the Noble Qur'an, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who takes you back at night, and knows what you have earned by day; then He resurrects you therein﴾ [Al-An'am: 60]. His saying ﴿then He resurrects you therein﴾ contains evidence for what al-Zamakhshari mentioned, because both ba'th (resurrection) and nushur are applied to life after death. And as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die during their sleep; then He keeps those upon whom He has decreed death and releases the others until a specified term﴾ [Az-Zumar: 42]. Al-Jawhari said in his "Sihah": "Al-masbut is the dead and the one who has fainted," end.

As for those who said that subat in the verse is rest brought about by sleep from the fatigue of work during the day, they said that the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and made the day a resurrection﴾ is that people disperse therein for their livelihoods, their earnings, and their means. Apparently this explanation involves an omitted genitive (mudaf), or it is of the type of the attributive masdar. This explanation is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We made the day for livelihood﴾ [An-Naba: 11], and His saying in "Al-Qasas": ﴿And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty﴾ [Al-Qasas: 73], meaning: that you may rest at night, and seek of His bounty by day in striving for livelihood.

When you know this, know that what this noble verse indicates has been made clear in other places, such as His saying: ﴿And We made your sleep a rest﴾, ﴿And We made the night a garment﴾, ﴿And We made the day for livelihood﴾ [Al-Qasas: 9–11], and His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you light? Will you not then listen?﴾ ﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you a night in which you rest? Will you not then see?﴾ ﴿And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ [Al-Qasas: 71–73].

And His saying: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs, and We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day illuminating, that you may seek bounty from your Lord and know the number of years and the reckoning﴾ [Al-Isra: 12], and We have explained this in our discussion of that verse.

And as in His saying: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾ ﴿and by the day when it appears﴾ [Al-Layl: 1–2], and His saying: ﴿By the day when it displays it﴾ ﴿and by the night when it covers it﴾ [Ash-Shams: 3–4], and other verses.

In the verses mentioned is a clarification that the night and the day are two of His signs and two of His blessings, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 48:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy﴾.

We have already presented the verse that clarifies this in Surah "al-A'raf," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds﴾ ﴿as glad tidings before His mercy﴾ [al-A'raf: 57], according to the reading of the one who reads bushran with a ba' (ب).

The verse of "al-A'raf" and the verse of "al-Furqan" that were mentioned indicate that rain is a mercy from Allah to His creation.

This has been explained in other places, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So look at the traces of Allah's mercy, how He gives life to the earth after its death﴾ [al-Rum: 50], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who sends down the rain after they have despaired, and spreads His mercy﴾, the verse [al-Shura: 28].

﴿And We have certainly distributed it among them that they might take heed, but most of the people refused except to be ungrateful.﴾

**Verification:** The pronoun in His saying ﴿And We have certainly distributed it﴾ refers to the rain-water mentioned in His saying ﴿And We send down from the sky pure water﴾, as related from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, Qatadah and others. This differs from those who said that the pronoun refers to the Qur'an, as related from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, which al-Qurtubi began with, and al-Zamakhshari began with something close to it.

Once you know that the verified view is that the pronoun in "We have distributed it" refers to the rain-water, then know that the meaning is: We have distributed the rain-water among the people, so We send down abundant rain in some years upon some lands and withhold rain in some years from some lands. Fertility therefore increases in some of them and drought in others. His saying ﴿that they might take heed﴾ means: We distributed it among them in order that they might remember. That is, those whose lands became fertile through abundant rain remember God's blessing upon them, so they give thanks to Him, and those whose lands were stricken with drought remember the affliction that befell them, so they hasten to repent to God, exalted is He, that He may have mercy on them and give them water. His saying ﴿but most of the people refused except to be ungrateful﴾ means: ungrateful for the blessing of the One who sent down the rain upon them, and that is by their saying: "We have been given rain by such-and-such a *nawʾ*" (the rising or setting of a star in its mansion, a pre-Islamic astrological notion).

This meaning, which this noble verse indicates, was also pointed to by God, exalted is He, in Surat "al-Waqi'ah," in His saying: ﴿And you make your provision [share] to be that you deny.﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 82]. So His saying "your provision" means the rain, as He said: ﴿And He sends down for you provision from the sky.﴾ [Ghafir: 13]. His saying "that you deny" means by your saying: "We have been given rain by such-and-such a *nawʾ*."

This is further clarified by the authentic hadith in Sahih Muslim, which we have already quoted in full with its chain and text: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions one day after a rain had fallen on them during the night: "Do you know what your Lord said?" They said: "God and His Messenger know best." He said: "He said: 'My servants have become, some believers in Me and some unbelievers. As for the one who said: "We have been given rain by the grace of God and His mercy," he is a believer in Me and an unbeliever in the star. As for the one who said: "We have been given rain by such-and-such a *nawʾ*," he is an unbeliever in Me and a believer in the star.'"

We have already stated that His saying in this noble verse, ﴿but most of the people refused except to be ungrateful﴾, includes the one who said: "We have been given rain by such-and-such a *nawʾ*," and the one who said: "We have been given rain by vapour" (meaning that water vapour rises from the sea, then gathers, then descends upon the earth by the necessity of nature, not by the action of any agent), and that the rain comes from it, as its explanation has already been set out. Exalted is He above what the wrongdoers say, a great exaltation.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 51:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And had We willed, We would have sent a warner to every town﴾ ﴿So do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with it, a great striving.﴾

(p-64) The meaning: Had We willed, We would have lightened from you the burdens of the message, and sent a warner to every town who would bear the hardship of warning on your behalf. That is: but We chose you and singled you out with the universal message to all people, magnifying your station and raising your rank. So you were met with ceaseless exertion and utmost firmness in conveying the message. And "do not obey the disbelievers" is the verse.

What this noble verse indicates of his ﷺ being chosen with the message for all people has been made clear in many verses, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾ [al-A'raf: 158]

• His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind﴾ [Saba': 28]

• His saying: ﴿This Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19]

• His saying: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud: 17], the verse.

We have already clarified this at the beginning of this noble surah, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [al-Furqan: 1]. And His saying "So do not obey the disbelievers" he also mentioned in other than this place, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾, the verse [al-Ahzab: 48]

• His saying: ﴿And do not obey from among them one who is sinful or ungrateful﴾ [al-Insan: 24]

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his desire﴾, the verse [al-Kahf: 28]

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not obey every habitual swearer, contemptible﴾ [al-Qalam: 10].

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿and strive against them with it﴾, that is, with the Qur'an, as was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas.

The great striving mentioned in this verse is that which is accompanied by harshness toward them, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who have believed, fight those adjacent to you of the disbelievers, and let them find in you harshness﴾, the verse [al-Tawbah: 123]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh with them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 73]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So do not obey the disbelievers﴾ — it is well known that he ﷺ did not obey the disbelievers, but he commanded and forbade in order to legislate for his ummah through his tongue, as we have explained in the surah of "Bani Isra'il".

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 53:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is He who let loose the two seas, one sweet and palatable, and the other salty and bitter; and He set between them a barrier and a forbidding partition.﴾

(p-65) Know that the word "maraja" (مَرَجَ) is used in the language in two senses:

The first: "maraja" meaning "to release and let be," from their saying: "maraja dabbatahu" (he let his animal loose) when he sent it out to the "maraj" (pasture), which is the place where animals graze; as Hassan ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

"And there was always a companion with her, amid its pastures, camels and sheep."

On this basis, the meaning is: He released the two seas and let them be, so that neither of them mixes with the other.

The second sense: "maraja" meaning "to mix," and from it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿in a confused matter﴾ (fi amrin marij), i.e., mixed up. According to the first view, the two seas refer to the sweet water in all of the world and the salt water in all of it.

His saying: ﴿This is sweet and palatable﴾ refers to the water of wells, rivers and springs in the regions of the world.

His saying: ﴿and this is salty and bitter﴾ means the salt sea, such as the Ocean and other seas that are salty and bitter. According to this interpretation, there is no difficulty.

As for the second view, that "maraja" means "mixed," the meaning is that in some places there occurs a mingling of salt water and sweet water in a single channel, yet neither mixes with the other; rather, there is a barrier between them by the power of Allah, may He be exalted. This is established as existing in some lands, and among the places where it occurs is the spot where the Senegal River mixes with the Atlantic Ocean beside the city of Saint-Louis. I visited the city of Saint-Louis in the year 1366 AH, and I bathed once in the Senegal River and once in the Ocean, but I did not reach the place of their mingling. However, some trustworthy companions informed me that he went to the place of their mingling, and that he was sitting scooping with one hand sweet and palatable water, and with the other salty and bitter water, while all of it was in a single channel, with neither mixing with the other. Glory be to Him, exalted is He; how great He is, and how perfect is His power.

What He, exalted is He, mentioned in this verse has been clarified in other places, such as His saying, may He be exalted, in Surat Fatir: ﴿And the two seas are not alike: this one is sweet and palatable, pleasant to drink, and this one is salty and bitter.﴾ [Fatir: 12] And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting together; between them is a barrier which they do not transgress.﴾ [al-Rahman: 19–20] (p-66) i.e., neither of them oversteps against the other so as to mix with it. This barrier separating the two seas, mentioned in Surat al-Furqan and Surat al-Rahman, Allah, may He be exalted, has explained in Surat al-Naml that it is a barrier by which He separated them, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is He who made the earth a resting place, and made rivers within it, and made for it firm mountains, and set between the two seas a barrier? Is there a god with Allah? Nay, most of them do not know.﴾ [al-Naml: 61] This barrier is the dry land separating the sweet water from the salt water according to the first interpretation.

As for the second interpretation, it is a barrier from the power of Allah, not visible to humans, and He emphasized the strength of its separation between them by His saying here: ﴿and a forbidding partition (hijran mahjura)﴾. The apparent meaning is that His saying here, "hijran," means a prohibition and a decreed prohibition, and "mahjuran" is an emphasis on it, i.e., a strong prevention of mingling between them. His saying "hadha 'adhbun" (this is sweet) is an adjectival form (sifa mushabbaha) from their saying: "adhuba al-ma'u" (the water became sweet) with a damma, so it is "adhbun." His saying "furat" is also an adjectival form, from "furita al-ma'u" with a damma, so it is "furat," when it is extremely sweet. His saying "wa-hadha milhun" (and this is salty) is also an adjectival form, from their saying: "malaha al-ma'u" with a damma or a fatha, so it is "milh."

Al-Jawhari said in his "Sihah": "mali^h" is not said except in a poor dialect, end quote.

Some have permitted it, and cited as evidence the words of the poet:

"Even if she spat into the sea, and the sea is salty, the water of the sea would become sweet from her saliva."

His saying "ujaj" is also an adjectival form, from their saying: "ajja al-ma'u yauiju ujuijan," so it is "ujaj," i.e., salty and bitter. The description of it as "ujaj" indicates an increase in bitterness beyond being salty. And knowledge is with Allah, may He be exalted.

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 25, verse 54:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is He who created from water a human being and made him [a line of] lineage and marriage. And your Lord is ever Competent.﴾

Al-Zamakhshari said in *al-Kashshaf*, in his explanation of this noble verse: He divided mankind into two categories: those of lineage (*dhawi nasab*), that is, males to whom lineage is traced, so it is said: "So-and-so son of so-and-so," and "So-and-so daughter of so-and-so," and those of marriage (*dhawat sihr*), that is, females with whom one becomes related by marriage. This is like His saying: ﴿So He made of him two sexes, the male and the female﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 39], ﴿and your Lord is ever Competent﴾, since from a single drop He created a human being of two kinds, male and female. End of his words.

This explanation that he gave of the verse is supported by what was cited as evidence for it, namely His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Did he not used to be a sperm-drop emitted [into the womb]?﴾ ﴿Then he became a clinging clot, and He created and proportioned [him]﴾ ﴿And made of him two sexes, the male and the female﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 37–39]. This is evidence that the verse of *al-Furqan* is clarified by the verse of *al-Qiyamah* that was mentioned. There are other opinions regarding this noble verse besides what al-Zamakhshari mentioned.

Among them is what Ibn Kathir mentioned, who said: ﴿And made him [a line of] lineage and marriage﴾: he is, at the beginning of his affair, a child of lineage, then he marries and becomes related by marriage. See the remaining opinions on the verse in the tafsir of al-Qurtubi and in *al-Durr al-Manthur* of al-Suyuti.

Issue.

Some scholars deduced from this noble verse that a man's daughter born of fornication (*zina*) is not forbidden to him in marriage (*nikah*). Ibn al-'Arabi the Maliki said regarding this verse: Lineage (*nasab*) is an expression for the mixing of water between the male and the female in the manner prescribed by the Law (*shar'*). If it occurs through disobedience, it is merely creation without established lineage. For this reason, his daughter from fornication does not fall under His saying: ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters﴾ [al-Nisa': 23], because she is not his daughter in the more correct of the two opinions of our scholars, and the more correct of the two opinions in religion. If there is no lineage in the Law, then there is no marriage relationship (*sihr*) in the Law, so fornication does not make forbidden [a man's] stepdaughter, nor the mother of a daughter. What is forbidden of the lawful is not forbidden of the unlawful, because Allah bestowed favor upon His servants through lineage and marriage and raised their status, and tied the rulings of permissibility and prohibition to them. Therefore, falsehood does not attach to them, nor does it equal them. End of his words, as transmitted by al-Qurtubi from him.

Al-Qurtubi said: The jurists differed regarding a man's marrying his daughter from fornication, or his sister, or his son's daughter from fornication. Some forbade that, among them Ibn al-Qasim, and this is the view of Abu Hanifa and his companions. Others permitted it, among them 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Majishun, and this is the view of al-Shafi'i. This has already been discussed in detail in *al-Nisa'*. End of his words.

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him and forgive him, says: The disagreement on this issue is well known and famous. The stronger of the two opinions in terms of evidence, as it appears, is that fornication does not make lawful things forbidden. So his daughter from fornication is not his daughter in the Law. Scholars have agreed that she is not included in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females﴾ [al-Nisa': 11]. The consensus (*ijma'*) is that she does not inherit, and she is not included in the verses of inheritance. This is clear evidence that she is a stranger to him, and not a daughter in the Law. However, what appears to us is that it is not appropriate for him to marry her under any circumstances. This is for two reasons. The first: that her being created from his water makes her closely resembling, in outward form, his daughter in the Law, and this strong resemblance between them should restrain him from marrying her. 

The second: it is not appropriate for him to take pleasure in something whose cause of existence was his disobedience to his Creator, may He be glorified and exalted. Regret for committing the sin, which is a pillar of repentance, does not suit taking pleasure in what arises from the sin itself. As for what he reported from al-Shafi'i, that he says the daughter from fornication is not forbidden, it is what al-Zamakhshari meant by his saying:

*"Even if I am a Shafi'i, they say of me that I permit marriage to the daughter, while the daughter is forbidden."*

* *

Note.

Know that what the author of *al-Durr al-Manthur* reported from Qatadah, which implies that he derived from His saying in this verse, ﴿and made him [a line of] lineage and marriage﴾, that marriage is like lineage in prohibition, and that each of them makes seven women forbidden, is a matter whose basis is not clear to me. What makes it even less apparent is the weakness of the indication by juxtaposition (*dalalat al-iqtiran*) according to the scholars of the principles of jurisprudence (*usul al-fiqh*), as its explanation has been set out repeatedly before. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 25, verse 55:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they worship besides Allah that which neither benefits them nor harms them﴾.

Its clarification has already been given in Surat al-Hajj and elsewhere. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the disbeliever is ever a helper (zahir) against his Lord﴾. The word zahir in the language means a helper, and from it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the angels, after that, are supporters﴾ [At-Tahrim: 4], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "My Lord, because You have bestowed favor upon me, I will never be a supporter of the criminals"﴾ [Al-Qasas: 17].

The meaning of His saying in this noble verse, ﴿And the disbeliever is ever a helper against his Lord﴾, according to the most apparent of the opinions, is: the disbeliever is a helper to Satan and his party from among the disbelievers against the enmity toward Allah and His messengers. So the disbeliever who is of Satan's party fights in Satan's cause against the friends of Allah, who fight in the cause of Allah. Thus the disbeliever assists Satan and his party in their endeavor so that the word of Allah would not be the highest. This meaning is indicated by verses of the Book of Allah, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of Taghut. So fight against the allies of Satan﴾ [An-Nisa: 76], and so on. It is known that the one who fights in the cause of Taghut, against those who fight in the cause of Allah, is a helper against his Lord.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they have taken besides Allah gods, that perhaps they might be helped. They are not able to help them, while they are for them an army brought forward﴾ [Ya-Sin: 74-75]. According to the view of those who said that the "army brought forward" are the disbelievers, who fight on behalf of their gods and defend them, whoever fights on behalf of the idols, defending their worship, is a helper against his Lord. His being a helper against his Lord means: an assistant to Satan and his party against the enmity toward Allah and His messengers, just as being an enemy to Him is mentioned in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers and Jibril and Mika'il - then indeed, Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 98], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Day when the enemies of Allah are gathered to the Fire, they will be driven in order﴾ [Fussilat: 19]. It is known by necessity that if all of creation cooperated in enmity toward Allah, they could not harm Him at all; they would only harm themselves thereby: ﴿O mankind, you are the poor toward Allah, and Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fatir: 15].

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We did not send you except as a bringer of good news and a warner.﴾

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And put your trust in the Living, who does not die﴾.

We have already mentioned the verses clarifying the like of this in Surah "al-Fatihah" (the Opening), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is You we worship, and You we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And sufficient is He as Knower of the sins of His servants﴾.
